Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 1:

(p-402) Surat al-Hashr

Its purpose is to explain what the end of al-Mujadila indicates of His transcendence above every flaw of deficiency, by affirming His all-encompassing power, with visible evidence that He overcomes, He and His messengers, and whoever opposes Him is among the most abased, because He is Strong and Mighty. This entails complete knowledge, which entails [perfect wisdom], which entails the gathering (hashr) that manifests the success of the successful and the ruin of the ruined, in a manner of permanence that reveals, most completely, all attributes of perfection. The most indicative of what it contains of this is contemplating the story of [the Banu] al-Nadir, which informs of the first gathering and announces the true gathering through the power to effect it after both friend and foe had agreed it would not occur. Therefore it is named after the gathering and after the Banu al-Nadir, because He, glorified and exalted, gathered them by His power from the blessed city of Madina to Khaybar, Syria and al-Hira; then He gathered [others] of the Jews too, from Khaybar to Syria, the second gathering, which is the sign of the Greatest Gathering, to the land of the gathering, to subdue through this noble Prophet the People of the Book, who claimed to be the best of people (p-403) and that they are supported by their religion, whose origin is upright, as the iron hinted at. Just as he subdued the people of idols, who knew that they had altered the true religion, it was established, by the manifestation of his religion over every religion on an equal basis, as He, glorified be He, promised, the truthfulness of His word in all that He brought after tawhid: belief in the Last Resurrection, because it is the locus of wisdom and the place where vengeance and mercy are made manifest.

"In the name of Allah" the Greatest King, whose command none can repel, so there is no breaking of His promise to His servants; "the Most Gracious" whose blessing of creation is universal, so there is no escape from His return; "the Most Merciful" who singled out those who love Him with success in what pleases Him from them, which necessitates for them the triumph of His felicity.

* *

When al-Mujadila concluded with Him being the Strengthener of those who obey Him and the Humiliator of those who disobey Him and oppose Him, He gave the reason for it through His transcendence above deficiencies, as confirmation of the promise of their victory, saying: ﴿Sabbaha﴾ i.e. He effected the greatest glorification (tanzih) above every flaw of deficiency, ﴿lillah﴾ (for Allah), who encompasses all [attributes of] perfection.

Since the disbelievers of all the children of Adam worshipped some the sun (p-404) and some the moon and some [other than these] of the stars, and the stars were scattered throughout all the heavens, not specific to one heaven, and likewise the angels, He used the plural as a sign that all are servants, saying: ﴿mā fī as-samāwāt﴾ i.e. all of them. Since the discourse concerns the prohibition of befriending those who oppose Allah, and that applies to those beneath the sincere ones, He emphasized by repeating the negation due to their need for emphasis, saying: ﴿wa mā﴾. Since all that they worshipped of what they associated with Him, from earthly things such as trees, idols, cows and others, does not exceed the earth on which they stand, He used the singular, saying: ﴿fī al-ard﴾.

Since this encompassed the whole world, He indicated that His greatness has no limit, saying: ﴿wa Huwa﴾ i.e. and the state is that He alone is ﴿al-ʿAzīz﴾ (the Mighty), who overcomes everything, and nothing is beyond Him, ﴿al-Ḥakīm﴾ (the Wise), whose knowledge penetrates the outward and inward and encompasses everything, so He perfects what He wills; everything He created He made a proof of His oneness, and a way to show what He has of might and wisdom.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: There is no obscurity in the connection of ʾayyuhā (as in ﴿yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū﴾) with what came later in the verses of Surat al-Mujadila. Do you not see that His saying, exalted be He, ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies a people upon whom Allah has become angry﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 13], is only meant as the Jews? So He mentioned the evil of their inner nature and their great audacity. Then He said at the end of the surah, ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22]. From all this there resulted (p-405) the warning of the believers against them and informing them that hatred of them is part of faith and friendship with them is part of hypocrisy, because of the ugliness of what they concealed and the monstrousness of what they committed. When these verses pointed to what was mentioned, they were followed, at the beginning of Surat al-Hashr, by the announcement of what He hastened for them of their humiliation, their expulsion from their homes and their wealth, and the empowerment of the Muslims over them, in continuation of what had been alluded to earlier regarding their evil conduct. The verses were joined by unity of meaning and its harmony, and the interweaving of the discourse. The surah opens with glorification because it is built upon what His anger toward them indicated, for that can only be in response to the greatest crime and the worst transgression, which is their aggression and disobedience, detailed in several places of the Book. He, exalted be He, said about them after mentioning His anger toward them: ﴿Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 60]. And He, exalted be He, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That is because they disobeyed and were aggressing﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 78]. So He made clear that His curse upon them was only consequent upon their disobedience and aggression, and He also detailed their aggression in several places. Since the anger indicated what was mentioned of great shirk, He, glorified and exalted be He, followed it with the glorification of Himself, saying: ﴿Glorifies Allah whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. Such glorification only occurs after a crime committed by the servants and a great sin they commit; reflect on that wherever it occurs. Then the discourse returned to informing of what He, exalted be He, did to the People of the Book, which is connected to what preceded. Then the verses were interwoven, ending.

(p-406) When he (exalted is He) declared His own absolute holiness, He indicated that holiness, and His might and wisdom, through an observed proof: that He carried out what He had decreed, namely that He and His messengers would prevail; that He humiliated those who opposed Him; and that He frustrated the expectations of the hypocrites. They had allied themselves with the Jews from among the People of the Book in order to gain strength through them, so He abased the Jews and expelled them from the place of the revelation's descent, and He disgraced the hypocrites who had made the Jews their basis of reliance, the object of their allegiance and affection. Then He said: ﴿He it is﴾, that is, He alone, without any cavalry or camel riding having been needed, ﴿who expelled﴾ by way of subjugation ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who concealed what was in their scriptures of the evidences bearing witness to Muhammad ﷺ as the final Prophet, and what was in their original nature that following the truth is more deserving. He also denounced their disbelief by saying, in place of "from the Banu al-Nadir" or "the Jews" for example: ﴿from among the People of the Book﴾, that is, the one which Allah revealed to His messenger Moses (may Allah's blessings be upon our Prophet and upon him, and grant him peace). The use of the verb "disbelieved" indicates that they are the ones who, through alteration or concealment, removed what they could of the Torah that testified to the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.

Since the homeland is the counterpart of the soul, for it is to the body what the body is to the soul, leaving it is extremely difficult. So He indicated the greater degree of their subjugation by it, saying: ﴿from their homes﴾. Some of them migrated from the blessed city of Medina to Khaybar, namely the family of Abu al-Huqayq and the family of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, while the rest joined Jericho in the land of al-Sham, the land of the Gathering, and some joined al-Hira. (p-407) He thereby alluded to the conquest of Khaybar and to their being gathered out of it in a second gathering, by saying, giving the reason or the time: ﴿at the first gathering﴾, that is, for the first gathering, or at the first gathering. This also indicates that every land to which they were gathered would be conquered, and that they would be shaken with another quaking, and their calamities against the people of Islam would not cease until the Greatest Gathering on the Day of Resurrection. "Gathering" means assembling from a place and driving to another against one's will. It was called the first because they were the first of the Jews to be expelled from the Arabian Peninsula. The second gathering of them from Khaybar took place in the time of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him). According to Ibn Ishaq, their expulsion occurred upon the Prophet's ﷺ return from Uhud, and the conquest of Qurayza upon his return from the Confederates, and between the two were two years. "The Prophet ﷺ said to them: Leave. They said: To where? He said: To the land of the gathering." Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: "Whoever doubts that the gathering is in the land of al-Sham, let him recite this verse." End of quotation. This gathering points to the Greatest Gathering, and the Prophet ﷺ clarified it in his saying: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two."

(p-408) Since He had informed that their gathering had not occurred through any cause other than His pure power, He resumed explaining this by saying: ﴿You did not think﴾, that is, O believers, ﴿that they would go out﴾, that is, that they would bring about the departure from a thing you had inherited from them, given your weakness and their strength in their numbers, their fierce might and their resoluteness, and the proximity of the Banu Qurayza to them, so that they were in a position to back them. The people of Khaybar were also not far from them, and all of them were of their creed, while the hypocrites were their helpers and kin. Yet their expectations were frustrated in all of that, their opinions were rendered worthless, and the believers prevailed over them despite their fewness and weakness. When Allah wishes to grant victory to a servant, his hare becomes a lion; and when He wishes to subdue an enemy, his lion becomes a she-camel.

Since fortresses prevent [the enemy] until reinforcements arrive, He said: ﴿And they thought that they would be protected﴾ and, to indicate the strength and firmness of their conviction, He expressed it by a nominal sentence, saying: ﴿their fortresses protecting them﴾, that is, protection is established for them and resistance belongs to them. The scholars said: placing the predicate before the subject indicates their excessive confidence in the strength of these fortresses and their protection of them. And in making their pronoun the subject of (inna) and attributing the sentence to it, there is evidence of their conviction, regarding themselves, that they were in (p-409) a state of might and invulnerability with no hope of overcoming them. It also indicates the weakness of their intellects, in that He referred to His army by His name and by His greatest name, saying: ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, from the Greatest King, besides whom there is no might, while you are His soldiers who fight only for Him and through Him; your might comes from His might. Thus the two presumptions converge on one thing. Since attributing what belongs to the genitive to the one it is genitive of is common in the speech of the Arabs, and very frequent because it is not confused by one who has familiarity with their speech, and very eloquent because of the grandeur it carries, He said: ﴿Then Allah came to them﴾ [Aal ʿImran: 148], that is, the Greatest King came to them, whose coming they could not bear, with what their own wretchedness had depicted for them, which compelled them to leave. ﴿From where they did not reckon﴾, that is, from the direction they had not prepared themselves for, namely the abandonment of the hypocrites, terror like their terror, and weakness like the weakness of their own selves, against resisting the soldiers of Allah. This was after Satan had made other things appealing to them and filled their hearts with empty desires, until they were certain of what he had promised them, what he had brought near to them, and what he had deluded them with.

Since the sense was: "Then Allah weakened them thereby," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And He cast﴾, that is, He sent down with a descent as if He had hurled it with stones, so it settled and took root ﴿into their hearts terror﴾ (p-410), that is, the fear which dwelt in them, shattering and filling them, passing from them to all their powers, and uprooting them from their foundations. Then He clarified their state at that point, or explained the casting of terror, by His saying: ﴿They were destroying their houses﴾, that is, they were exaggerating, according to the reading of Abu ʿAmr with the doubled letter, in ruining them, meaning corrupting them, for "kharba" means corruption. The reading of others conveys the unrestricted act, which does not contradict the restricted one. ﴿With their own hands﴾: out of weakness on their part, indicated by the plural of paucity, and out of despair of their own strength, so that they could take whatever they found valuable from their materials. Thus a man among them, when they were preparing to depart, would tear down his house from its doorframe and take whatever wood he found valuable, placing it on the back of his camel and carrying it away; he would breach the wall and bring down the roof, out of envy toward the Muslims lest they dwell in them after them. This was because the Prophet ﷺ had ordered them to vacate the city for him, and they were allowed to take what their camels could carry.

Since the cause of the Companions' (may Allah be pleased with them) ruin of their houses was the deceit and treachery which the Jews had used against them, they were as if the Jews had commanded them to do that, so the Companions acted in that capacity on their behalf. Therefore He said again, using the plural of paucity to indicate that the act belongs to Him alone (glorified is He): ﴿and the hands of the believers﴾, that is, those firmly established in faith, by taking control and overpowering them. The believers had been demolishing whatever narrowed their room for fighting. He placed (p-411) their demolition first because it is more striking.

Since it is extremely strange for a person to do to himself what his enemy does to him, He based on this His saying: ﴿So take warning﴾, that is, make yourselves diligently reflect on the immense power of Allah the Exalted, so that you may cross from the outward aspects of knowledge in this matter to the inward wisdom of what Allah arranged in their expulsion. Do not count any helper for yourselves from creation, and do not rely on anyone other than Allah. For taking warning, as al-Qushayri said, is one of the principles of the Law (sharʿ), and whoever does not take warning from others will have others take warning from him. End of quotation. The verse has also been used as evidence by the upholders of qiyas (analogical reasoning), since it is a passage from the original case to the derivative case, and such passing over is a form of i'tibar (taking warning/inference), which is commanded in this verse, and so it is obligatory.

Since taking warning is of great benefit and is attained only by the perfected, He magnified it further by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O people of vision﴾, by considering with your eyes and your insights this strange act, so that you may realize what He promised you through the tongue of His messenger ﷺ, namely the manifestation of His religion and the exaltation of His Prophet. Do not rely on anyone other than Allah as these people relied on the hypocrites, for whoever relies on a created being will be left by that to his own humiliation and degradation. Do not be inclined toward treachery as they wished to betray the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, planning to cast upon him, while he was sitting in the courtyard of one of their houses, a millstone from the roof in order to kill him with it, so they claimed. Do not commit any of their ugly deeds, lest there come upon you the like of their punishment (p-412), as His saying ﷺ confirms: "You will certainly follow the ways of those who came before you," etc. That treachery from them came after they had incited Quraysh to the battle of Uhud and directed them to some weak points. Al-Baghawi said: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Quraysh after Uhud with forty riders and allied with them against the Prophet ﷺ. Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended to him informing him of this. He said: When he (peace be upon him) went toward them, they sent to him to come out with thirty men, and thirty of them would come out to listen to him; if they believed in him, all would believe. He agreed, but they then sent word that the gathering was large, so he should come out with three, and three of them would come out. A woman among them then sent to her brother, who was a Muslim, that they had concealed daggers intending to assassinate the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he ﷺ refrained from that. Everything mentioned among the causes of their story [as you see] revolves around deception; indeed it is the very essence of deception.

Now when this showed the extent of their weakness, which made it a matter for wonder that they were not killed, he explained that the reason for this was His overpowering command and His dominant might, urging reflection, contemplation and insight, the lesson with which he concluded the previous verse. So He said: ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed﴾, that is, had prescribed as an absolute obligation, the King to whom belongs all command (p-٤١٣), and it indicates that He decreed it as humiliation and disgrace by His saying: ﴿upon them﴾, that is, specifically for them, in what He had decreed from eternity (al-azal, pre-eternity) for the Children of Israel, just as He decreed it for Banu Qaynuqa', ﴿exile (al-jala')﴾, that is, leaving their homes and wandering in the land. As for most of them, Bukht Nasr (Nebuchadnezzar) exiled them from the lands of al-Sham to Iraq. As for these, Allah protected them from that exile through the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and made it come about at the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he exiled them. Some of them went to Khaybar and some went to al-Sham, time after time. ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾, that is, with the sword, as He will do to their allies from Banu Qurayzah, upon whom He decreed the punishment rather than exile, namely the killing of the fighting men and the taking captive of the offspring. For He, exalted is He, has decreed with an absolute decree that He will purify the city, the land of revelation, of them.

Since the implied sense was: "But He decreed this for them, so it is their punishment now in this world without doubt, even if the people of the earth unite to support them," he followed it, by way of mockery (al-tahakkum) through the use of a particle of benefit, with His saying: ﴿And for them﴾, that is, in any case, whether they are exiled or left, ﴿in the Hereafter﴾, which is the abode of permanence, ﴿is the punishment of the Fire﴾, and that is the greater punishment.

When he had informed them of what befell them in this world and what awaits them in the Hereafter, he gave the reason for it with His saying: ﴿That﴾, meaning the matter [the great one] which He did to them of exile (al-jalāʾ) and its preliminaries [in this world], and which He will do to them in the Hereafter, ﴿because they﴾. Since they had added to the open disbelief they already held a hidden disbelief, through what they intended of casting the millstone and other harm, as a scheme on their part, he assimilated (idghām) the letters in His saying ﴿opposed God﴾ (شاقّوا), meaning the Supreme King, who has complete encompassing power. Thus they were on a side other than His side, having moved to the side of the enemies who wage war, after having been on the side of those with whom a truce had been made.

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went along with their concealment of what they intended to do to him, by concealing his own plan for his escape from them, by returning to the noble city of Madinah and leaving his Companions, may God be pleased with them, among them, He said: ﴿and His Messenger﴾, whose honouring is part of honouring Him. When He had informed of their act and its cause, He joined to it, as an emphasis on its meaning and an added benefit, because He does to others who follow their course something greater than their own act, His saying: ﴿And whoever opposes God﴾, meaning whoever brings about within himself opposition to the Supreme King, who has no equal, in the present, the past, or the future, whether or not he conceals another opposition alongside it. He left the assimilation (idghām) in its original form, because they did not openly show hostility; what they did was a scheme and concealment, and that is lighter than open defiance. He used the full form in al-Anfāl (وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ اللهَ) because of the strength of the matter of those who defied openly, as has passed. He did not repeat the mention of the Messenger, to magnify him by conveying that opposing him is opposing God, without any separation at all. It also indicates that they went to great lengths in concealing their opposition, so that God alone became aware of it, and therefore there was no mutual interaction (mufāʿala) between them and the Messenger (ﷺ) in that matter, for he did not scheme against them. Rather, he confronted them openly when God informed him of their scheme. This differs from what preceded in al-Anfāl, where the context required mention of the Messenger, because they schemed against him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ [al-Anfāl: 30], and so on. He (ﷺ) concealed the matter of his migration and employed a stratagem to escape their scheme, in accordance with what God had commanded him, so the mutual interaction (mufāʿala) occurred in each of the two parties moving secretly to a side other than the side of the other. ﴿Indeed, God﴾, meaning the One who encompasses all greatness, intensifies His punishment for him ﴿because He is severe in retribution﴾. This is as He did to the Banū Qurayẓah after this, when they broke their covenant and openly showed opposition during the Battle of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb), and as He did to the people of Khaybar. They used to scheme and conceal in the first case at its conquest and in the second at their expulsion from it. Thus He equated those who concealed with those who openly defied in punishment, though it is clear that the punishment for the openly defiant is more severe.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 5:

When Allah, glorified is He, had shown His might and wisdom through what He did to the Banu al-Nadir, who used to say that they were the bravest of people and the most stubborn of them, by reason of their nobility and their being chosen above the worlds, along with being supported by the Book and wisdom, and He concluded by saying that whoever opposes His Messenger, then indeed He has opposed him, and whoever opposes Him, then His punishment is severe, He followed this with an explanation of what He punished them with, namely the cutting down by the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, by the command of the Prophet ﷺ, of their palm trees, which were dearer to them than their firstborn, while they were watching it, unable to avail anything, and having no defence before them. So He said: ﴿Whatever﴾, and it is a conditional particle, and He followed it with its conditional verb which governs it, so He said: ﴿you cut down﴾, meaning, everything you cut down. He clarified the vagueness in "whatever" by His saying, describing the palm trees in a manner that indicates their type and that cutting them down was easy and gentle for them: ﴿of palm trees (lina)﴾. It is a kind of palm tree. Ibn Ishaq said: it is what differs from the ajwa (a type of date palm). Ibn Hisham said: al-lina is among the varieties, and it is that which is neither barniyya nor ajwa of the palm trees, as related to me by Abu 'Ubayda, end of quote. The author of al-Qamus said: al-lawn is the dagl (inferior dates) of the palm trees, and they are a group, whose singular is lawna and lina. Al-Mahdawi said: it is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, and Mujahid [and others], that it is all of the palm trees. Al-Baghawi said: the narration of Zadhan from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Prophet ﷺ [used to cut] their palm trees except the ajwa." The people of Madina call the dates other than the ajwa al-alwan, whose singular is lawn and lina. 'Atiyya, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Zayd and 'Amr ibn Maymun said: al-lina is the palm tree; the two are names with one meaning, and its plural is lin and liyan. Sufyan al-Thawri said: al-lina is that whose dates are lawn, a type of date that is intensely yellow, through which the seed is visible from outside. Al-Baghawi said: the molar tooth disappears into it, and it was among their finest dates and most pleasing to them. One single palm tree's price was the price of a servant dearer to them than a servant. When they saw them cutting it down, it grieved them, and they said to the believers: "You dislike corruption, yet you are causing corruption; leave this palm tree, for it belongs to whoever overcomes it." Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': the variation of colours in it is apparent, for at its beginning it is white like a shell filled with pearls arranged in rows, then grey, then green as if they were pieces of emerald in which water has been created, then red as if they were rubies packed one upon another, then yellow as if they were a fragment of gold; and therefore when half of it reaches the stage of ripening it is called mujazza'a (variegated) because of the variation of its colours, as if it were the Dhafari onyx.

Since the thing explained by the feminine noun is the lina, He returned the pronoun in the feminine, so He said: ﴿or you left it﴾. And since leaving (al-tark) applies whether it remains standing planted or cut, He said: ﴿standing﴾. And since the intended meaning is many palm trees, given the intention of the genus, He said: ﴿upon their roots﴾, using the plural of multiplicity. ﴿So by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning, so its cutting was by the empowerment and approval of the Supreme King. Al-Qushayri said: in this is evidence that the Sharia is not rationalized, and when a legal command comes, the seeking of a reason ceases, and the tongues fall silent from interrogating with "why," and the presence of objection and deeming it ugly in the mind is a departure from the limit of gnosis.

Since He weaned them from seeking causes, addressing the perfected ones, He comforted the hearts of those below them with a cause conjoined to what is implied: "So that is not corruption, but it is righteousness which He permitted you in, in order to heal the breasts of the believers and remove the rage of their hearts." So He said, placing an apparent noun in the place of their pronoun, which indicates what made them disgraced: ﴿and that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾, those who are deeply rooted in going out of the circle of truth, by humiliating them and exposing them, through making clear their falsehood in their claim to might, bravery, and support from Allah, because they are upon the true religion, and that it does not admit abrogation. Abu Ya'la related from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "He permitted them to cut palm trees, then made it stricter upon them, so they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah! Is there sin upon us for what we cut, or upon us for what we left? So Allah revealed the verse." End of quote. Some of the believers inclined toward refraining from cutting because of what the Jews called corruption, and a group advised continuing the cutting because it enraged them. So Allah, glorified is He, approved in the verse of the one who ordered refraining and absolved of sin the one who advised continuing the cutting. The verse thus indicates the permissibility of corrupting the property of the people of war in any state, whether it bears fruit or not, by burning, drowning, demolishing, and otherwise, in order to disgrace them thereby.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 6:

Since the spoils that are divided among the army are only what they fought for, whereas what comes without fighting is *fay'* (property acquired without battle, which the imam takes and divides into five parts), he divides it into five-fifths. Then he divides one fifth of it into five shares. The first of these, which belonged to the Prophet ﷺ and after him goes to the public interests of the Muslims, and the other four shares of this fifth go to those mentioned in the verse after it. The four-fifths that make up the original division, which were for the Messenger of God ﷺ, because they were obtained through his sufficiency and by striking terror into the enemy, are distributed among the mercenaries from all regions. So all wealth belongs to God, as a favour to those who worship Him by what He has prescribed through the tongues of His messengers, peace be upon them. The wealth of the disbelievers was in their hands as usurped property that they had seized [p. 420] from its rightful owners. God, glory be to Him, singled out the Messenger of God ﷺ with the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir, to place it wherever he wished, because it was *fay'*. So He said: ﴿And what God restored﴾, that is, the King to whom all command belongs restored it with ease, after it had apparently been in the utmost difficulty and hardship, ﴿to His Messenger﴾, so He placed it in his hand after its being removed from it by the disbelievers laying hands on it unjustly and aggressively, as the term *fay'* indicates, which is the return of the shadow to the side from which it began. ﴿From them﴾, that is, a restoration that began from the corrupt ones. Thus He made clear that this is *fay'* and not *ghanimah*. The property of those among them who died without an heir also falls under *fay'*, as does the *jizyah*. As for *ghanimah*, it is what is taken by fighting and by the charging of horses and camels.

Since war is only a matter of attack and retreat, with swiftness, lightness and agility, deception by horsemen, evasion by the brave, and raiding by people of striking and thrusting, He said, giving the reason for its being *fay'*: ﴿So you did not press forward﴾, that is, you did not hasten. Ibn Ishaq said: "You did not stir up or pursue on the march" — end of quote. That pressing forward was for the purpose of prevailing ﴿over it﴾. He intensified the negation with the prepositional phrase and said: ﴿with horses﴾, and he emphasised it by repeating the negative, because of those who thought it was *ghanimah* since they had encircled them, so He said: ﴿nor camels﴾, that is, riding camels, which were specially designated among mounts. Nor did you cover a distance for its sake, so you did not undergo great hardship in seizing their wealth, because their town was in the status of the blessed city of Madinah. There was no distance between it and what lay adjacent to it, but it was contiguous to one of the villages of the Ansar, of which Madinah is the name as a whole. It was the village of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf in Quba', between them and the village where the Messenger of God ﷺ was staying, a distance of about two miles. So everyone went on foot, and none rode except the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they did not fight there in any battle afterward. For this reason God made it *fay'* and did not make it *ghanimah*. So it is divided according to the division of *fay'*, not the division of *ghanimah*. Its fifth goes to the recipients of the fifth of *ghanimah*, who are the five categories mentioned in the verse after it, and what remains, the four-fifths, belongs to him ﷺ, added to what he had taken from the fifth of the fifth.

Since the meaning of this is: the domination was not by you, He corrected it with His saying: ﴿But God﴾, that is, He to whom all might belongs, so there is no equal to Him, ﴿gives power to His messengers﴾, that is, this is His custom in every age, ﴿over whom He wills﴾, by making the awe that He gave them a terror in the hearts of His enemies. He it is who gave his messenger ﷺ power over these people by casting into his blessed mind that he should go to them and ask them for help with the blood money for the two men of the Banu 'Amir whom 'Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri, may God be pleased with him, had killed by mistake. When the Messenger of God ﷺ sat beside one of their houses, and they had been under a truce with him ﷺ, they secretly broke their covenant out of deceit, after welcoming him and promising him help. They ordered one of them to drop a rock on him from the roof so as to kill him. [God] informed him of this, so he went away and left his companions there until they caught up with him. This came after Huyayy had done what he did: going to Makkah and urging the Quraysh to war against the Prophet ﷺ, and making a pact with them that he would be with them against him, peace be upon him, and God informed His Messenger ﷺ of this. So he sent to them after morning: "You have betrayed God and His Messenger, and you intended to do such and such. The land belongs to God and His Messenger, so leave it, and I give you a term of ten days." They remained for some days preparing for departure. Ibn Ubayy and those with him among the hypocrites sent to them that they would be with them in adversity and in ease and would not abandon them. Ibn Ubayy said: "I have two thousand men of my people and others of the Arabs who will enter your fort, and they will die to the last of them, and Qurayzah and your allies of Ghatafan will support you." Huyayy ibn Akhtab was tempted by this and sent back: "We will not leave our homes, so do what you will." The Messenger of God ﷺ marched against them with the believers, his banner carried by 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. He prayed the afternoon prayer in their courtyard after appointing Ibn Umm Maktum, may God be pleased with him, over Madinah. He remained over them for six nights while they were fortified. He cut down some of their palm trees and burned [them]. They called out to him: "You used to forbid corruption and blame those who did it, so why are you cutting down the palms?" They awaited the help of Ibn Ubayy and those with him [p. 423] regarding what they had said, but they did not fulfil it for them. God then cast terror into their hearts, so they sent a reply agreeing. He said: "No, unless you give me your weapons, and whatever wealth of yours you cannot carry on your camels." They hesitated, then agreed, and they carried from their wealth as much as the camels could bear, except for the armour, and they went away with six hundred camels. They displayed their jewellery and fine garments, and their women revealed their adornments. Some of them joined Khaybar and some went to Syria, and they left the property and the armour to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Of them only two men became Muslims, Yamin ibn 'Amr and Abu Sa'd ibn Wahb, and they became Muslim while keeping their property, so they secured it. God made the property of those among them who did not become Muslim *fay'* belonging to the Messenger of God ﷺ alone, to place it wherever he wished, as is related in the Sahih from 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, in the story of the dispute between 'Ali and al-'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. In it he said that this was among his special privileges ﷺ, for he said: "God singled out His Messenger ﷺ in this *fay'* with something He gave to no one else," then he recited ﹛And what God restored to His Messenger from them﹜ up to His saying ﹛Powerful﹜. "So it was exclusively for the Messenger of God ﷺ. By God, he did not hoard it away from you, nor did he monopolise it over you; he gave it to you and distributed it among you, until this wealth remained from it" — meaning the wealth over which their dispute had arisen. The Messenger of God ﷺ used to spend on his family the provision for their year from this wealth, then he would take what remained and place it where the things of God are placed. And also in the Sahih, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, from 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, who said: "The property of the Banu al-Nadir was among what God restored to His Messenger ﷺ, which the Muslims had not pressed forward against with horses or camels, so it was exclusively for the Messenger of God ﷺ; he spent from it on his family the provision of a year, then he placed what remained in weapons and horses as provision for the cause of God." End of quote. The Messenger of God ﷺ divided their wealth, after keeping for himself what he kept, among the emigrants, and gave the Ansar nothing from it except three men who were in severe need: Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, Sahl ibn Hunayf and al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, may God be pleased with them. [The sword of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq had a reputation among them, so he gave it as a special award to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may God be pleased with him.] Al-Isfahani said: during the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, *fay'* was divided into twenty-five shares: four-fifths of it, which is twenty shares, belonged to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who did with them as he wished and decided concerning them as he willed. The remaining fifth was divided as the fifth of *ghanimah* is divided, that is, among the Messenger of God ﷺ, the near kin, and those after them. This was his practice ﷺ [with his special properties, (p. 425) and when he died it went to the Imam of the Muslims, and so did all that the Messenger of God ﷺ left], because he said: "We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity." Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, then took charge of it, followed by 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, and they both did with it what the Messenger of God ﷺ had done. Al-Isfahani also said, may God be pleased with him, citing Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, may God be pleased with him: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, recited ﹛The alms are only for the poor﹜ [al-Tawbah: 60] up to ﹛Knowing, Wise﹜ [al-Tawbah: 60], then said: "This is for these," then he recited ﹛And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God﹜ [al-Anfal: 41], then said: "This is for these." Then he recited ﹛What God restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﹜ [al-Hashr: 7] up to ﹛for the poor emigrants﹜ [al-Hashr: 8], ﹛and those who were settled in the abode and in faith﹜ [al-Hashr: 9], ﹛and those who came after them﹜ [al-Hashr: 10]. Then he said: "This has comprehended all the Muslims in general, so no one is excluded but has a right to it. If I live, the herdsman will certainly receive his share of it without sweating his brow over it" — end of quote.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: what the Prophet ﷺ took from the Banu al-Nadir and from Fadak is specific to the Prophet ﷺ, and it does not follow the rule of *ghanimah*, which is taken by pressing forward and fighting. The school of al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, is that these properties, which are *fay'*, are like the rest of *fay'*, divided into [five] shares: a fifth of them goes to the categories mentioned, the first of whom is the Prophet ﷺ, and the four-fifths belong to him ﷺ alone. Al-Shafi'i answered the saying of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, (p. 426) "it was exclusively for the Messenger of God ﷺ," that it is a general statement meaning a particular one, and its meaning is: what remained of it in the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ, after giving the fifth to its recipients, was exclusively his ﷺ. No one doubts his exclusive entitlement to it. Moreover, he did not hoard it away from them, but rather he did what is mentioned in the hadith of preferring others to himself. Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said: "We have no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ gave the categories mentioned in the verse their rights from it, and we know that the right of these categories from the property of the polytheists is the fifth, as is explicit in Surah al-Anfal. It is inferred from 'Umar's saying, 'It was for the Prophet ﷺ,' that he had what the Muslims share in [from the fifth of the *ghanimah* obtained through the terror that came upon the disbelievers from them, and what the Muslims share in after the fifth is the four-fifths]. The Prophet ﷺ stood in the place of the Muslims in it, since they had not pressed forward against it with horses or camels. It came about only through the terror that God cast into the hearts of the polytheists for His Messenger ﷺ. So the four-fifths are restricted to those who were the cause of obtaining the whole [as in *ghanimah*, so on this view *fay'* and *ghanimah* do not differ in that the four-fifths are restricted to whoever was the cause (p. 427) of obtaining the whole], and that the fifth of both kinds of property goes to the categories mentioned. What he ﷺ had of *fay'* from the four-fifths will, after his death ﷺ, go to the fighters, because it was obtained through the terror that came upon the disbelievers from them, just as the four-fifths of *ghanimah* were obtained through fighting them."

Since His power, glory be to Him, is general in giving power and in everything else, He made it manifest and did not leave it implicit. So He said: ﴿And God﴾, that is, the King to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿is over all things﴾, that is, any thing to which the will may validly attach, which is every possibility of giving power and other things, ﴿Powerful﹜, that is, His power reaches to the furthest ends. The verse indicates that pressing forward with horses and camels and making for distant places against the enemy has a great effect upon souls and a tremendous terror.

When God removed their wealth from the hands of the army, He explained the disposal of other property of the same kind, that which was given to him ﷺ without fighting. He said, beginning a new sentence as an answer to one who might ask: "Does this ruling apply to every fay' (booty obtained without battle) that comes after Banu al-Nadir?" ﴿What God has restored﴾, that is, the one who is singled out for might, wisdom and power, ﴿to His Messenger﴾. Since He, glorified is He, fully knew that He would give His Messenger power over the people of Wadi al-Qura and others greater than this power (p-428), He said, so that it would be one of the signs of prophethood: ﴿from the people of the towns﴾, that is, the town of Banu al-Nadir and others from Wadi al-Qura, al-Safra', Yanbu' and the other Arab towns there that are called the Arab towns. ﴿is for God﴾, that is, the Supreme King in whose hand is all affairs, ﴿and for the Messenger﴾, because he is the greatest of His creation, so his rank follows His rank. These two appear to be separate shares, but they are not; they are one share. However, He mentioned His own sacred Self for blessing, since every matter not begun with Him is cut off, and to honour His Messenger ﷺ, to inform that he has no personal desire at all in anything of this world. Rather, his pleasure is the pleasure of his Lord; his character is the Qur'an, which is the attribute of God, and he is its manifestation and its display. His share ﷺ is, after him, spent on the welfare of the Muslims, such as weapons, frontier posts, scholars, judges and imams.

When this statement had made clear to the Messenger of God ﷺ such virtue and greatness that cannot be described, He followed it with another honour by honouring his relatives for his sake. For this reason He repeated the governing particle and said: ﴿and for the near of kin﴾, that is, of his, because their rank comes after his rank. They are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, the kin (rahṭ) of our imam al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, the rich and the poor among them alike, because their taking of this share is by kinship and not by need, as is the position of Imam al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him. When He mentioned the people of honour, He followed them with the people of weakness, to console their frailty, and He said, putting the weakest first: ﴿and the orphans﴾ (p-429), [that is] those who are most in need of compassion, because the foundation of the religion is to adopt the character of God, of which the most important is strengthening the weak and mending the broken; ﴿and the needy﴾ [for they are] in weakness [next after them]. The poor are included among them, for when the term "poor" (faqir) or "needy" (miskin) is used alone, each of them includes the other; they are distinguished only when both are mentioned together. Likewise, fay' and ghanima (spoils taken by force), when mentioned separately, may each include the other; but when both are mentioned together, fay' is what is obtained without fighting and without the pressing of horses and camels, while ghanima is what is obtained by that means. ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, who are the strangers, cut off from their homelands and their kin. The division of fay' among these categories, as has passed, is that it is divided into five parts: one fifth of it is for the Messenger of God ﷺ, [and] those created beings mentioned with him, and God is mentioned among them for blessing, because the categories mentioned are those expressed by His name, glorified is He. The remaining four-fifths are exclusively for him ﷺ; from them he spends the maintenance of a year, and what remains beyond that he spends on the welfare of the Muslims: weapons, [horses] and the like. Whatever belonged to him ﷺ during his lifetime is for the public good after his death, just as he used to do with what exceeded his needs. Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said [in al-Umm]: Whatever is taken from a polytheist (p-430) by any means other than the hospitality of Muslims who pass by them is of two kinds, from neither of which it departs. Both are explained in the Book of God, the Exalted, and in the sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ and in his practice. The first is ghanima. God, the Exalted, said in Surat al-Anfal: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty - indeed, for God is one fifth of it and for the Messenger﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. The second is fay', and it is divided in the Book of God in Surat al-Hashr. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And what God restored to His Messenger from them﴾ [al-Hashr: 6] - to His saying - ﴿Kind and merciful﴾ [al-Hashr: 10]. These two kinds of property are what God has granted to whomever He has made it for from among the people of His religion, and these are properties which the rulers must manage; they cannot leave them alone. Ghanima and fay' are alike in that both contain together a fifth of each, for those whom God, the Exalted, named, and those whom God named in the two verses [together] are alike, joined and not separated. Then the ruling differs concerning the four-fifths by what God, the Mighty and Majestic, explained through the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ and in his practice. For he divided four-fifths of ghanima, and ghanima is what is obtained by pressing with horses and camels, among those who were present, rich and poor alike. Fay' is what was not obtained by pressing with horses or camels. So the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ regarding the villages of 'Urayna, which God restored to him, was that four-fifths of them belonged exclusively to the Messenger of God ﷺ, to the exclusion of the Muslims, and the Messenger of God ﷺ placed it wherever God, the Mighty and Majestic, showed him. Then he mentioned the hadith of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, may God be pleased with him, concerning the dispute of 'Ali and al-'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Al-Shafi'i said: The property of Banu al-Nadir which God restored to His Messenger ﷺ, concerning which 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, spoke, is what remained of it in the hand of the Prophet ﷺ after the fifth and after things which the Prophet ﷺ distributed from it among men of the Emigrants; he gave none of it to any Ansari except two men who mentioned poverty. This is explained in its proper place. In this hadith is evidence that 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, only reported that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and he (p-431) approved what remained of these properties which had been in the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ, in the manner in which they saw the Messenger of God ﷺ acting with them, and that neither of them had, from what the Muslims had not obtained by pressing, any share of fay' that belonged to the Messenger of God ﷺ; they were only among the Muslims in it on equal terms. That was their conduct and the conduct of those after them. The matter on which none of the people of knowledge among us disagreed, as far as I know, and which has continued to be preserved in their statements, is that no one has what belonged to the Messenger of God ﷺ of the choice portion of the booty (safi) or of the four-fifths of what was not obtained by pressing. And the maintenance which the Messenger of God ﷺ used to provide for his wives and others, if they were with him, has passed; I know of no one among the people of knowledge who said that the heirs of these had that maintenance which they had. There is no dispute that those maintenance payments are to be applied where the Prophet ﷺ used to apply the surpluses of the income of those properties, in what serves the welfare of Islam and its people. Al-Shafi'i said: The jizya is part of fay', and its path is the path of all that is taken from a polytheist's property by pressing, that a fifth of it is taken, for those whom God, the Mighty and Majestic, named, and four-fifths of it are as I will explain, if God, the Exalted, wills. Likewise, everything taken from a polytheist's [property] without pressing; this is like what is taken from him when he dies in the lands of the Muslims and has no heir, and other than that which is taken from his property. In the time of the Prophet ﷺ there was fay' other than the villages of 'Urayna, such as the jizya of the people of Bahrain and Hajar and other than that, and for him ﷺ four-fifths of it, to be given wherever God, the Mighty and Majestic, willed, and the one whom God made entitled to the fifth received his fifth. End of quotation.

When He, glorified is He, had ruled this ruling concerning fay' which opposed what they were upon (p-433) in the Jahiliyya, namely the exclusive possession of it by the rich, He explained its cause, which makes manifest His greatness, glorified is He, and the excellence of His management and mercy. He said, linking it to what the preposition was linked to: ﴿So that it will not be [a perpetual] circulation﴾, that is, the fay' which God, glorified is He, drove by His power and which He specially gave to His Prophet ﷺ, by casting terror into the hearts of his enemies, and which by right should be given to the poor, ﴿a circulation﴾, that is, something taken by the wealthy and the noble by way of domination and overpowering, a jahili (pre-Islamic) selfishness. This is the reading of the majority. Abu Ja'far and Hisham, on the authority of Ibn 'Amir, read with a feminine verb from the complete "kana" and "dulah" in the nominative, as its subject, ﴿among the rich from among you﴾, passing it round among themselves, for they used to say: "from the mighty." From this al-Hasan said: "They took God's servants as servants and God's wealth as passed around," meaning whoever prevailed among them took it and monopolized it. It was said: the dammah (u) is a name for what is passed around, like ghurfa (a handful) is a name for what is scooped, while the fatha (a) is the act of passing around.

Since the estimation was: "So do what I have commanded you concerning its division, for those I have commanded," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you﴾, that is, everything that he brings to you and enables you to have, ﴿take it﴾, that is, accept it, accepting it as one who has acquired it; ﴿and whatever he forbids you﴾ of all things, ﴿refrain﴾, because he does not speak from desire and does not say or do anything except what his Lord has commanded him. Whoever accepts this, affairs become easy for him, as has been transmitted: "The Qur'an is difficult and hard to bear for one who abandons it, and easy for one who seeks it and follows it." It is reported that the verse (p-434) was revealed concerning some people of the Ansar who said: "We have our share of these towns."

Since restraint from what souls have become accustomed to is difficult, especially when it involves enjoying wealth in the manner of leadership, He warned against opposing this by His saying: ﴿And fear God﴾, that is, make for yourselves, by obedience to the Messenger of God ﷺ, a shield against the punishment of the greatest King, who encompasses all in knowledge and power. He gave the reason for this by His saying, magnifying Him by repeating the divine name, emphasizing it, because the act of the one who opposes is the act of one who denies: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, the One to whom alone belong majesty and honour absolutely, ﴿is severe in punishment﴾, that is, the punishment which falls after sin. Whoever claims that anything in this surah has been abrogated (naskh, the replacement of a ruling by a later one) by something in Surat al-Anfal has erred, because al-Anfal was revealed concerning Badr, and [it] came a period before this.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 8:

When He, glory be to Him, had removed the spoils of war (fay') from the hands of those who had them and from the customs they followed in the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance), and had explained the disposition of the fay' among the people of the towns, and had threatened those who opposed this in that matter, because it is hard on souls, it was fitting that it be accepted after He had made clear that the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir belonged to whomever He had given authority over them, namely His Messenger (ﷺ). It was known from his (ﷺ) condition that he preferred others over himself and was content with only what sufficed him. After making clear that his (ﷺ) needs were provided for, He explained the manner of its disposal, because explaining that was the greatest aim, since it was present and at hand, the prepared path for it being the wealth of the people of the towns. So He said, with ﴿for Allah and the Messenger﴾ [al-Anfal: 24] and what is conjoined to them in apposition [min] (p-435), because whoever gives to the emigrants (muhajirun) for their emigration and their stripping away of their wealth and homes, has given it for the sake of Allah and the face of His Messenger (ﷺ). It is not in apposition to ﴿the near kin﴾, lest it be restricted to their poor. Or it is a reply to one who seems to have said: "We have heard and obeyed; so for whom is what Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) have given authority over of their wealth?" So it was said to him: ﴿for the poor﴾, meaning those of them who, when a man would tie a stone to his belly from hunger, and dig a pit in winter to protect himself from the cold, having no covering other than it, after having had wealth sufficient for him and surplus from which he could support others. He described them with poverty only because they were in that state at the time of its revelation. Then he specified them by a description, saying: ﴿the emigrants﴾. Since emigration (hijra) may be applied to one who abandons the people of disbelief without leaving his homeland, He said: ﴿who were expelled﴾, and He put it in the passive form, because what matters is the expulsion itself, not that it came from a specific expeller, ﴿from their homes﴾. Since expulsion here implies the sense of prevention, and the expression with it was chosen [as a sign] that wealth is a covering for a person, since it is his container, He said: ﴿and their wealth﴾ (p-436). Since seeking the world is among the defects, He made clear that if it comes from Allah it is not so, and that it does not harm sincerity, and that the matter of the Banu al-Nadir was only made easy to bring about the fulfilment of their hope. So He said: ﴿seeking﴾, meaning [they were expelled] while they were seeking, with diligent effort. He made clear that nothing is obligatory upon Him toward anyone by His saying: ﴿a bounty from Allah﴾, meaning the Greatest King, to whom none is equal, because He is singled out for all attributes of perfection in this world, the religion and the Hereafter; so He enriches them by His bounty, independent of anyone else, ﴿and good pleasure﴾, He guides them to what pleases Him concerning them, and does not make their desire for reward from Him harmful to sincerity, so He brings them to the abode of His honour.

When He had described them as having their inner selves attached to Him, glory be to Him, and severed from everything else by their contentment with the expulsion, He described them by offering up their outward selves to Him, saying: ﴿and they help﴾, [meaning] in a manner of renewal at every time and continuity, ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the Greatest, the Glorious King, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, whose greatness is part of His greatness, with their persons and their wealth, so that the party of Satan may be annihilated. When the care He, glory be to Him, has for them was made manifest, the listener awaited, in their praise, what befits this report.

Then He said, beginning a new sentence which is like the cause for their being singled out: ﴿Those﴾, meaning those high in rank in noble character, ﴿they are﴾ (p-437), meaning exclusively, not others, ﴿the truthful﴾, those most firmly rooted in this quality, because their emigration for what was mentioned and their abandonment of what was described indicate the perfection of their truthfulness in what they claimed of faith in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), since they cast off those who opposed both, even the close relative pure of lineage and home, and they preferred as allies those whom both of them had, however far their home and distant their dwelling. This indicates that the foundation of religion is establishing proofs by steadfastness against trials, and that help may come in proportion to the trial, because Allah, exalted is He, has singled out the emigrants from what He permitted of the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 9:

When He praised the Muhajirun (the Emigrants) and gave to them, the souls of the Ansar (the Helpers) were content with that. They were, in every state, with him (ﷺ) like the corpse before the washer, who does whatever he wills, and whatever he wished from them, he reached and attained. So He followed their praise, as consolation for them and as thanks for their deeds, saying, joining it to the whole account: ﴿And those who had settled [in the city] before them﴾. That is, they made every effort to make ﴿the abode﴾ (the perfect abode among abodes) which Allah had prepared from eternity for the hijrah (emigration), and readied for the victory, and made encircling all the lands, surrounding them, prevailing over them: the place of their residence, their association, their companionship and their attachment. This is because it is fit that whoever left it should return to it, so that he would never abandon it at all. It is the place of his longing, and it is not (p-438) a place one emigrates from for its blessing or its goodness.

Since the purpose was to make the praise of them complete, He said, implying in ﴿settled﴾ a necessary meaning: ﴿and the faith﴾. That is, they were in intimate attachment to it, kept company with it, devoted themselves to it, and clung to it with a clinging like the clinging to a dwelling without which its occupant cannot do. It is permissible that [the faith] be a description of the abode, by repeating the conjunction to indicate the firm establishment in each of the two attributes, so that it is as if it were said: they settled in Medina, which is the abode and which is the faith, because it is the place of the firm establishment of faith, of its spread and of its manifestation throughout the lands. Because of its intense association [with faith], it was named after it. It is also permissible that the meaning is: and the place of the faith, indicating that they did not remain in it for the sake of their wealth being in it, but out of love for the faith, knowing that its full moon could not be complete, its nobility and worth could not be perfected, its banners could not be spread, nor its remembrance strengthened, except by it. Had it not been so, they would have abandoned it and emigrated to the Prophet (ﷺ) wherever he settled. So this is a praise of them: that they are characterized by the hijrah in potential, together with their being characterized by the nusrah (support) in actuality.

Since their exclusive establishment of the faith in the mentioned abode before the arrival of the Emigrants upon them was a complete praise, He said, praising them by this, indicating by the affirmation of the preposition that they did not exhaust the time of the period before, from the moment the Messenger (ﷺ) was sent, with both matters: ﴿before them﴾, that is, before the emigration of the Emigrants, because their description with hijrah did not exist except after its establishment. So the Ansar combined the firm establishment in faith with the firm establishment in the abode, before the Emigrants combined the two by the hijrah.

When He began their mention with this sublime beginning, He informed about them by His saying: ﴿they love﴾, that is, in a manner of renewal and continuity. It was said that it is a conjunction upon the Muhajirun, and this is a state, so this would be a judgment of sharing: ﴿whoever emigrated﴾. He increased them in love for them and compassion toward them with His saying: ﴿to them﴾, because intending a person necessitates his right over oneself, since were it not for the perfection of one's love for him, one would not single him out with the intention toward him. The witnessed evidence for what Allah informed about them of love is that they shared their wealth with the Emigrants and offered them that they share their wives with them, despite the intensity of their jealousy, but the Emigrants refused sharing in the women and accepted the wealth from them.

When He informed them of the love and encouraged them to sustain it, He joined to this report what is among its fruits, so He said: ﴿and they do not find﴾ [that is] at all ﴿in their breasts﴾, which are the dwellings of their hearts, from which the commands of the hearts issue, let alone that their tongues should utter [it]. Since the purpose was the negation of seeking from them what was specific to the Emigrants, and the impelling cause for seeking that is need, and since every person dislikes being attributed to need, even if he reports it about himself at some time for a purpose, He said: ﴿need﴾, placing the name of the cause for the effect, ﴿of what they were given﴾, that is, the Emigrants, from the fay' (spoils without battle) and other [than it], from the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir and others, from any giver whatsoever, so how much more when the giver is Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). And if they do not find a need that calls them to seeking, then all the more they do not find envy or rage, by way of a fortiori. So this verse is among the greatest incitements to good brotherhood and a warning against envy and resentment. When He reported their being free of vices, He followed it with the report of their adornment with virtues, so He said: ﴿and they prefer﴾. He magnified this by restricting the verb, so the meaning becomes: they bring about al-athara (preference), which is choosing good things for others, singling them out with them, not for their loved ones for example, but ﴿over themselves﴾, so they give to others, whoever they may be, what is in their hands. The mention of the self is evidence of their being in the utmost purity from vices, because when the self is purified the heart is purer. He emphasized that with His saying: ﴿even though﴾, that is, a state that is at its utmost limit of need ﴿they themselves﴾, that is, specifically, not by the one preferred ﴿had poverty﴾, that is, destitution and deficiency in circumstances and a severe need surrounding them from every side, from the gaps of the structure, and [it] is its openings.

Since the estimation was: whoever is like this is among the truthful, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And whoever﴾. Since the aim is purity from vice from whatever direction it comes, and the treatment of vices is extremely difficult, which a person cannot bear except with a severe help from Allah, He put into the passive form His saying: ﴿is protected from the avarice of his soul﴾, that is, a shield is established between him and his blameworthy characters, referred to by the self, which stands between him and them, so that it does not hinder what is in his hand, nor is he greedy for what is in the hand of another out of envy. Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: avarice is that a man's eye aspires to what is not his. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of avarice, for it destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was forbidden to them."

Since the consideration [of] purification from base morals is great, He made its result follow as a clarification, because what it causes does not come about without it, [with His saying]: ﴿those﴾, that is, those of high rank, ﴿they are﴾, that is, specifically and not others, ﴿the successful﴾, that is, the perfect in attaining every desire. [Al-Qushayri said: the stripping of the heart from worldly accidents and possessions is the attribute of the masters and the eminent. Whoever is captured by dangers and remains in the avarice of his soul is occupied with exchanging his dealings and demanding from people to take his share, and so he has no taste of this path at all.]

The explanation of the verse is that when the Emigrants came to the Ansar, the Ansar divided their homes and their wealth between themselves and them. When Allah bestowed upon His Messenger (ﷺ) the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir, the Prophet (ﷺ) gave a sermon, mentioning what they had done for the Emigrants of lodging them and preferring them over themselves (p-442). Then he said: "If you wish, I will divide between you and the Emigrants what Allah has bestowed upon me from the Banu al-Nadir, and the Emigrants would remain as they are, residing in your homes and with your wealth; and if you wish, I will give them and they will leave your dwellings." Then the two Sa'ds (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Rather, it should be divided among the Emigrants alone, and they would remain in our homes as they were." The Ansar said: "We are content and submit." And in another narration they said: "Divide it, this alone, and divide for them from our wealth whatever you wish." Then it was revealed:

﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves﴾ - the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, have mercy on the Ansar and the sons of the Ansar." Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "May Allah reward you with good, O assembly of the Ansar. By Allah, our likeness and your likeness is only as the Anazi said:"

Allah has repaid us on behalf of Ja'far when our sandal slipped among the trampling feet, and it slipped.

They refused to weary of us, and if our mother had encountered what they encounter from us, she would have grown weary.

By my life, they are truly deserving of the name of brothers of purity, friends of manliness and fidelity, of nobility and selection. May Allah be pleased with them and with their followers among the noble successors, the masters and the upright.

(p-443) When Allah, glorified and exalted, praised the Muhajirun (the Emigrants) and the Ansar (the Helpers), may Allah be pleased with them, for what they deserve, He followed with the Tabi'un (the Successors) who follow them in excellence, what calls for praise for them. He said, joining them to the Muhajirun, which implies association with them, or joining them to the main subject of the narrative as a conjunction of sentences: ﴿And those who came after them﴾, meaning from whatever group they were. Since what is intended is coming, even if only after a short time, He stated the preposition, saying ﴿after them﴾, meaning after the Muhajirun and the Ansar. They are those who believed after the cessation of hijrah (migration) with the conquest, and after the faith of the Ansar who embraced Islam after the Prophet (ﷺ), until the Day of Resurrection. Then He mentioned the predicate or the circumstantial clause in the manner that preceded in the previous verse, saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say﴾, meaning in a manner of continual renewal and persistence, confirming their faith, by their supplication for those who laid down this path for them: ﴿Our Lord﴾, meaning, O You who are good to us by bringing into existence those who prepared the religion before us. Since a human being, however much he strives, is a place for deficiency, He said, instructing us: ﴿Forgive﴾, meaning, cast a veil over the deficiencies, both their essences and their effects, ﴿us﴾. Since they began with themselves, they then mentioned those who were the cause of their faith, saying: ﴿and our brothers﴾, meaning in religion, for that is the greatest brotherhood, and they explained the reason with their words: ﴿who preceded us in faith﴾. Since He, glorified is He, taught them to show good succession to those who prepared for them what they are in, He followed it with teaching them how to deal with their helpers, those who are with them, in a way that encompasses those before them. So He said, informing that the whole matter is in His hand, urging them to seek refuge in Him from the dangers of the self, which is the most hostile of enemies: ﴿And do not place﴾. His saying ﴿in our hearts﴾ conveys that the vices of the self rarely disappear, and that if they exist alongside soundness of the heart, they are close to not having an effect. ﴿Ghillan﴾ (rancor), meaning spite, envy, and malice, and it is [heat and] a surging that necessitates vengeance, ﴿toward those who have believed﴾, meaning who have affirmed faith, even if they are at its lowest degree.

Since this is a supplication comprehensive of good, He taught them what would answer them if they adhered to it and adopted its character, along with what it contains of flattery toward the Deity and of hinting to Him with strength of hope. So He said: ﴿Our Lord﴾, meaning, O You who are good to us by teaching us what we did not know. They emphasized, to inform that they believe what they say, even if their actions sometimes manifest what discredits their belief, saying: ﴿Indeed You are Ra'uf﴾, meaning most merciful, with the utmost mercy, to whoever has a connection to You through an act of goodness, ﴿Raheem﴾, honouring to the utmost degree whomever You will, even if he has no connection. So You are worthy that You answer us, for we are either one who has a connection, and so are among the people of tenderness, or one who does not, and so are among the people of mercy. This verse has therefore established that whoever has rancor in his heart toward any of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, (p-445) is not among those whom Allah intended by this verse.

When this showed that this praise is for those who are truthful in faith, in establishing the Sunnah through emigration (hijrah), preference for others (iithar), and striving in supplication for those whose faith is clear, so that the path to security became easy through it, this excluded the hypocrites (munafiqun) and made it understood that they do not do this, because they have no firm root in the faith that would drive them to it. It pointed to their hypocrisy (nifaq), which necessitates their lying, with His words, completing the story and addressing the highest of creation, as an indication that the hypocrisy of these people is not fully known to anyone other than him (ﷺ), because of the subtlety of their deceit. He marvels at their condition in lacking firm roots despite the miracles and clear signs they see, and despite what they see of the believers' condition: the outpouring of mercy upon them through the facilitation of affairs, victory over the tyrants, turning away from this world while turning toward the Hereafter, and striving in the religion, which alone calls to faith, softens hearts, and makes realities clear in the utmost clarity. ﴿Have you not seen﴾, that is, have you not known with a knowledge that is in the strength of certainty, as if witnessed, O highest of creation? He indicated their distance from his lofty presence and his noble, precious station with the particle of ending, and so He, exalted is He, said: (p-446) ﴿those who practised hypocrisy﴾, that is, they displayed other than what they concealed. They displayed good and went to great lengths to hide their beliefs of evil, with the exaggeration of one who competes with another. They were Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions. They said: "Nifaq" is an Islamic term that the Arabs did not know before it. It is a metaphor taken from the action of the dhabb (lizard) in its nafaqa' and qasa'a (its two escape holes). He depicted their condition with His words: ﴿they say to their brothers﴾, that is, in allegiance to misguidance.

When He had gathered them together in disbelief, though they differed in concealment and open declaration, He described the open ones with a kind of concealment that would cause aversion toward them and decree the ruin of whoever befriends them. He said: ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, they covered the lights of the knowledge that had guided them to the truth. He specified them with what is more emphatic in censuring them, in that they went astray with knowledge, and so He said: ﴿from the People of the Book﴾. They were the Banu al-Nadir. He rebuked them for their lying regarding what they affirmed in the promise, since it falls within the scope of what is denied, in that they could not openly declare their disbelief, so how could they openly oppose their people, the Ansar, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was among them, in their saying: ﴿If you are expelled﴾, [that is,] by any expeller from their land, which is in the noble city of Medina, and you leave without fighting, ﴿we will surely go out with you﴾. So what was decreed against their brothers of expulsion became an omen, entrusted to their own speech.

(p-447) Since it was known [that the hypocrites have relatives among the great believers, and it was known] that they would stand against them in preventing them from standing with them, out of sincere advice to them and kindness toward them, and since the Banu al-Nadir's granting permission was weakening to that, they said, emphasising their being with them: ﴿and we will not obey anyone regarding you﴾, that is, regarding your forsaking. The meaning is that even if someone were supposed to be as close to you as the contained is to the container, we would not obey him in falling short in what pleases you, ﴿anyone﴾, that is, who asks us to forsake you, whether from the Messenger or the believers. They emphasised with their saying: ﴿ever﴾, that is, as long as we live. With this kind of resolve, the disbeliever deserves eternal abiding in punishment.

When they had put forward in their aid what was an omen deciding against them, they followed it with their saying: ﴿and if you are fought against﴾, that is, by any fighter whatsoever, and you fight and do not leave, ﴿we will surely help you﴾. The verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device of mutual omission): He mentioned expulsion first as evidence of its opposite second, and fighting second as evidence of the omission of its opposite first. The meaning of the verse is that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent to the Banu al-Nadir: "Leave my land and do not dwell with me. You have resolved to betray me, and I have given you a term of ten days. Whoever of you is seen after that, I will strike his neck." He then sent to them Ibn Ubayy with what has been mentioned.

When their saying was a statement that its hearer would judge to be true, in that (p-448) it was emphasised while being initiated without any question about it, He, glorified is He, made its state clear with His saying: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, they say that, while the one who encompasses everything in power and knowledge ﴿bears witness﴾ to what He knows of their inner thoughts in the unseen realm. Since some of those who hear their saying would deny that reality does not correspond to it, and since their failure to fulfil it was certain in Allah's knowledge, He applied to it what is applied only to what reality has revealed to be non-corresponding. He said, encouraging the believers to fight them, emphatically: ﴿Indeed, they﴾, that is, the hypocrites, ﴿are liars﴾. This is among the greatest proofs of prophethood, because it is a report of the unseen far beyond the usual, evidenced by what you thought they would go out, and then Allah made it certain soon after.

Since the lie in their statement consisted in reporting what would not happen, He explained it with His words, stressing it more emphatically than they had: ﴿If they are expelled﴾, that is, the Banu al-Nadir, by whatever expulsion it might be, ﴿they will not go out﴾, that is, the hypocrites, ﴿with them﴾, that is, out of zeal for them, for reasons known to Allah. ﴿And if they are fought﴾, that is, the Jews, by whatever fighter, so how much more so against the most courageous and most knowledgeable of creation (ﷺ), ﴿they will not help them﴾, that is, the hypocrites. Allah has spoken truly, and they lied in both matters together: the fighting and the expulsion. They neither helped them nor went out with them. That was among the signs of prophethood (nubuwwah, the office of prophet), and whoever was doubtful, let alone whoever was certain, knew by it the truthfulness of the speech concerning what did not happen and would not have happened even had it been otherwise, and how it would happen, when, in His saying the Exalted, ﴿And if they help them﴾, that is, the hypocrites, at any time whatsoever, ﴿they will surely turn their backs﴾, that is, the hypocrites and those whom they help. He belittled them with His saying ﴿the backs﴾. Since it was the custom of the Arabs to return to battle after fleeing, He made clear that they would have no return after this flight, however long the span, so He said: ﴿Then they will not be helped﴾, that is, no help will be renewed for either of the two parties, nor for either one of them, at any time whatsoever.
