And Allah, glorified is He, has spoken truly: the hypocrites and the Jews have remained in humiliation and still are.

Since it may be said that their withholding from aiding them is due to fear of Allah or something else of a pleasing nature, he gave a reason that negates this and shows that the focus of their attention is on what is perceptible, like cattle. So he said, emphasizing it for the sake of the fact that the people of hypocrisy deny this, as do those whose condition is close to theirs: ﴿Indeed, you﴾ O believers ﴿are more intense in fear﴾, meaning in terms of fear. The word ﴿fear﴾ (رَهْبَةً) is a tamyiz (specification, an accusative noun clarifying the comparison) transferred from the subject (mubtada'), meaning: your fear that is in them is more intense and greater, ﴿in their breasts﴾, meaning the Jews and those who support them, ﴿more than [fear of] Allah﴾, meaning the fear they display to you of Him, even if they mention Him with every one of His attributes. Their fear of you is thus a cause for them to display, out of ostentation before you, that they fear Allah.

Since this is among the matters at which the believer marvels, he explained it with His words: ﴿That﴾, meaning this strange matter, which is their constant and enduring fear of a weak creature like themselves who adorns it for them, and their lack of fear of the Creator, despite His greatness in His essence and His being independent of them, ﴿is because they are a people﴾ who, despite their strength, ﴿do not comprehend﴾, meaning no understanding arises for them at any time, because of their disbelief and their reliance on their own deceit, that would open their breasts so that they might perceive that Allah is the One who should be feared and no other. Rather, they are like animals with no regard for the unseen; they are only with what is perceptible. Fiqh (فِقْه, understanding) is knowledge of the meaning of speech, both its apparent clear sense and its hidden obscure sense, through quickness of insight and excellence of natural disposition.

[p. 450]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 14:

When He had informed of their fear, He indicated it by His saying: ﴿They will not fight you all together﴾, meaning that each of the two groups, the Jews and the hypocrites, or one of them, will not fight you. Since a thing may be stated while only part of it is meant, He confirmed the matter with His saying: ﴿all together﴾, meaning in a battle they intend openly, while they are gathered together, all of them, at some time and in some place, ﴿except within fortified towns﴾, meaning protected by the guarding of the streets (durub, which are the wide roads), with gates, trenches and the like, ﴿or from behind walls﴾, meaning surrounded by them, whether in a village or elsewhere, because of the intensity of their fear. By this he excluded what happens from some of them out of necessity, such as a small matter, and those among the people of Khaybar who would come down from the fortress to duel and the like, for that was not from gathering together. Or this may be specific to the Banu al-Nadir in this attack.

When it might be thought that this was from an inability inherent in them, He removed that with emphasis, to inform that it is one of the miracles of this religion: ﴿Their might is among themselves intense﴾, meaning their strength and the qualities in them through which punishment is inflicted. ﴿Among themselves is intense﴾, meaning that when they deliberate a matter, or when some of them fight others, they are bold against the believers, for what they see of their intensity and bravery when they fight the polytheists is not denied when fighting the believers. It is a dignity Allah honoured the believers with, containing one of the signs of prophethood, to strengthen their faith and raise their standing.

When the cause of the intensity was gathering together, He explained the two states of intensity and fear with His saying, addressing the Prophet ﷺ, indicating the intensity of what they show of familiarity (ilf) with one another: ﴿You think them united﴾, meaning the Jews and the hypocrites, O most exalted of creation, and O you who looks, whoever has that apparent compassion, ﴿all together﴾, because of what they are in of gathering [for defence], and from that the intensity arose, ﴿while their hearts are scattered﴾, meaning divided to the utmost division, and from that the fear arose. The cause of this scattering is the divergence of desires which has no unifying bond from the order of reason, like beasts, even if they gather in enmity against the people of truth, like the gathering of beasts in fleeing from the wolf. Al-Qushayri said: the gathering of souls together with the repulsion and divergence of hearts is the root of every corruption, the cause of every failure, and the inducement of the enemy's audacity, while the agreement of hearts, sharing one aim and equality of purpose, brings about every victory and every happiness.

When the greatest cause of division was weakness of reason, He said, giving the reason: ﴿That is because they are a people﴾, meaning, despite their intensity, ﴿who do not reason﴾. So they have no religion that unites them, since they know they are upon falsehood; they are captives of desires, and desires are in the utmost divergence. Thus reason is the foundation of unity, just as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, were in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, just as desire is the foundation of division.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 15:

Since the statement that they lack understanding was an assertion, he supported it with something observable, so he said: ﴿Like﴾, that is, their condition in their lack of comprehension, or rather their lack of reason, which resulted in their expulsion, this, and what caused it of their scheming, their treachery, and their reliance on Ibn Ubayy and those with him of the hypocrites, is like the condition of ﴿those before them﴾. Since inserting the preposition, together with its indication that the time before them was not entirely covered, implies nearness in time, he stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿shortly﴾. They were, as "Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, Banu Qaynuqa', of the Jews, of their religion, who showed fierce hostility when the Prophet (ﷺ) marched against them after the battle of Badr. He admonished them and warned them of Allah's might. They said: 'Do not let yourself be deceived, O Muhammad, that you met a people who were inexperienced and had no knowledge of war, so you prevailed over them. As for us, by Allah, if you fought us, you would know that we are the men.' Then they plotted against a woman among the Muslims, and they wanted her (p-454) to uncover her face, but she refused. So they tied the end of her garment beneath her head-covering, and when she stood up, her private parts were exposed, so she cried out. A man among the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) was jealous on her behalf, so he killed the Jew who had tied her garment, and they killed him. Their covenant was thereby broken, so the Prophet (ﷺ) brought the armies of Allah upon their stronghold, and Allah humiliated them, and they came down from their fortress to his judgment (ﷺ). They had been allies of Ibn Ubayy, but he did not avail them anything, except that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) [concerning] that he not kill them, and he insisted upon it until he refrained from killing them, so they departed from the blessed city of their own accord, without being driven out or compelled to leave by force."

Since it was as though it had been asked: "What was their outcome?", he said: ﴿They tasted the evil﴾, that is, the bad consequence and the ill end of ﴿their affair﴾ [in this world], which was their disbelief and their enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his party, who [are the party of] Allah. He called it "affair" because it was among the things they plotted. ﴿And for them﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, ﴿is a painful punishment﴾, that is, one of severe pain.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 16:

When Allah, glorified is He, likened the state of those (hypocrites) who obeyed Ibn Ubayy and those with him, who were the distant ones destined for the Fire, regarding their obedience to them, because of the distancing of the believers from them through Allah's distancing of them and the burning of their hearts because of that, together with what He had prepared for them in the Hereafter through the affair of Banu Qaynuqa', He likened the story of all of them to the story of (p-455) Satan [and] whoever obeyed him among humans and jinn. So He said, clarifying the meaning of what the last of the speech had settled upon: ﴿Like the example﴾, that is, the example of all those who promise victory and are deceived by their own promises, while knowing that Allah has written in the Remembrance, ﴿Verily I and My messengers shall prevail﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], in their breaking of the promise and their abandoning of them when the matter became real, is like the example of ﴿Satan﴾, that is, the one far from all good because of his distance from Allah, burning in His punishment. Satan here is like the hypocrites. ﴿When he says to man﴾, that is, to every person in whom there is wavering and agitation, and he here is like the Jews: ﴿Disbelieve﴾, that is, in Allah, by what [he had made] attractive to him and whispered to him of following desires, which took the place of a command.

Since man, by what assists Satan's adornment upon him from his desires, his portions and his dispositions, generally obeys his command, He said: ﴿So when he disbelieves﴾, that is, brings about disbelief in whatever manner it occurred, and the particle "fa" indicates his haste in following his adornment. ﴿He says﴾, that is, Satan, who here is an expression for the hypocrites, affirming for the one who relies on him what he had promised him, with a true reliance upon him and a denial that he would forsake him: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you﴾, that is, there is no connection between me and you in anything at all, supposing that this disavowal benefits him in any way concerning what the one commanded to accept his command deserved. And that (p-456) is a metaphor [for] his having acted toward him with turning away from him and persistence in everything that indicates his neglect of one who affirms disavowal from him. This is like what the hypocrites did with the Jews: they emboldened them to a matter that was forbidden, which was remaining in their land; then, when they raised war hoping for their help, the hypocrites, by their slowness toward them, acted as one disavowing them, and that was more severe upon them than if they had not given them hope of help, because this is in the position of their fleeing from them from the battle line, which necessarily entails their defeat. Then He gave the reason for the disavowal by His saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, that is, the King with whom no one has any command, so His assault cannot be withstood. Then He explained that by His saying: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, the One who brought them into existence from non-existence and nurtured them by that which indicates all the Most Beautiful Names and the Lofty Attributes, so no one of His creation suffices in anything for anyone except by His permission, and [He] does not forgive at all anyone who impugns His lordship, especially if he attributes it to other than Him. This is like what a person finds after falling into disobedience of remorse and bewilderment; when he finds that and resolves to repent, the disobedience adorns itself for him, makes the repentance difficult and hard for him, and emboldens him toward the same disobedience or toward something greater than it, and he continues thus until return becomes impossible for him, so his ruin is realized and the ruin of whoever led him into it. Therefore on account of that He made His saying the consequence of it:

﴿So it was﴾. Since placing a thing before its proper position necessarily startles a person into alertness, prompting him to search for the cause and creating eagerness for what is delayed, He said: ﴿their end﴾, placing it first as the predicate (khabar, the complement) of the verb "كان" (kāna, "was"), ﴿that they both﴾, i.e., the deceiver and the deceived, ﴿are in the Fire﴾, the state being that ﴿they abide therein forever﴾, because they both did wrong [ظُلْمًا] (ẓulman, a wrong) "ظَلَما" (ẓalamā) with which there is no success.

Since this might be taken to refer to one particular person, He said, attaching it to the description as a generalization and a deterrent: ﴿And that﴾, i.e., the greater punishment, ﴿is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., of every [one] who places worship in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 18:

When the Exalted had drawn out the admonitions in this surah both in word and in deed, and the calamities mentioned in it were caused by betrayals from those who had a covenant and broke it, or from those who had professed faith and whose actions revealed their lie, He, glorified and exalted be He, said, by way of deduction from that and as an admonition to the believers, because admonition after calamities falls more heavily upon the soul, is greater in softening the heart, and in warning it against what brings punishment: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, calling them with the call of distance, describing them with the lowest degree of faith, because it follows the mention of those who professed only with their tongues. ﴿Fear Allah﴾, that is, make for yourselves a protection that will shield you from the wrath of the Supreme King, beside whom no one has any command, and before whom everyone must surely be presented as His servants. So beware of His punishment on account of falling short in what He has set as limits for you of command or prohibition. ﴿And let every soul look﴾, that is, let every soul look at what it has put forward, and it desires to be exalted over its peers; and perhaps He made it singular (nafs) to indicate, together with the generality it conveys, how very few are those who comply with this command. ﴿what it has put forward﴾ (p-458), that is, of the provision by which the abode is set right; whoever does not strive to set it right will have no rest. Will what it has put forward please the King, so that it saves it, or will it anger Him, so that it destroys it?

Since the term of life is undetermined in time, and meeting Allah is, for the intelligent person, awaited every day and indeed every moment, since it is possible [along with being] absolutely [certain] and known to no one as unknown, He said, indicating by its indefiniteness and vagueness its grandeur and magnitude: ﴿for tomorrow﴾, that is, for the sake of the reckoning after death, or on the Day of Resurrection, which is in extreme nearness, because this whole worldly life is one day in which some people come and others go; death or the Hereafter is its tomorrow, and there must be one of these two. Whatever must be is in extreme nearness, especially if it is lasting and not ended. Whoever looks to his tomorrow has best observed the care of his today. Its tanwin (indefiniteness) is for magnification in countless respects.

When He, glorified be He, commanded them to fear Him out of dread of His might, He commanded them to fear Him for the sake of watching over Him, out of shame before His majesty and awe, as an emphasis on the matter, because the basis of salvation rests on piety, since the snares of Satan are subtle. Whoever does not strive hard in calling his soul to account and in scrutinizing whatever deficiency may exist in his deeds is close to having Satan nullify his deeds. So He, exalted be He, said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, the One who combines all attributes of perfection; that is, fear Him out of shame before Him. The first piety is for bringing the forms of deeds into being, and this one is for purifying them and cleansing their spirits. For this reason He gave the reason in His words (p-459), encouraging and warning: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong the most beautiful names and the highest attributes, ﴿is Acquainted﴾, that is, of great awareness of your outward and inward states and encompassing of ﴿what you do﴾. So you do no deed except that it is in His sight and hearing, so be shy before Him. He repeated the greatest Name, lest it be thought that piety is restricted to a particular respect among the respects, magnifying this station, informing that His affairs are not confined, that His encompassing does not single out one station over another nor one matter apart from another.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 19:

When He stirred them toward their taqwa (God-consciousness, piety) at one time through fear and at another through shame, as a reinforcement of it, and gave the reason for that by what has an aspect of warning, and since man, because of his forgetfulness, is more in need of warning, He said, reinforcing that aspect and clarifying that the second taqwa is for taking account of the self in purifying the deed: ﴿And be not like those who forgot God﴾, O you who need warning, and they are those who believed, ﴿like those who forgot God﴾, that is, they turned away from His commands and His prohibitions and abandoned them as the abandonment of those who forget, toward One from whom (commands) have departed, although He possesses the attributes of majesty and generosity, because Satan led them astray through His command until he removed them far from the dwelling place. ﴿So He caused them to forget themselves﴾, that is, as a consequence of that, He caused them to forget themselves, by His encompassing of the outward and the inward, ﴿themselves﴾, so they did not send forward for themselves what would benefit them; and if they did send forward something, it was mixed with corrupting things, such as showing off (riya') and self-admiration (ujb). So they were of those of whom He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be humbled﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 2], ﴿labouring, weary﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 3], ﴿burning in a scorching Fire﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 4], ﴿given to drink from a boiling spring﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 5], because they left no door of wickedness unopened; for the head of wickedness is ignorance of God, and the head of knowledge and the key to wisdom is knowledge of the self. Whoever knows himself knows his Lord: "Whoever knows himself, knows his Lord."

Since the fruit of that was that they wasted it, that is, taqwa, and so they perished, He said: ﴿Those are﴾, that is, those far from every good, ﴿they are﴾, that is, exclusively and not others, ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, those who are most deeply sunk in going out of the circle of religion.

When the proof was complete that the Party of God (ḥizb Allāh) are the successful (al-mufliḥūn), because of what He strengthened them with in this worldly life, namely victory and firmness against the enemies, gentleness and mutual support toward the allies, and all the other deeds that lead to the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma’wā), and when He stated explicitly at the end of the proof the loss of the Party of Satan (ḥizb al-shayṭān), it became known that for them, along with this humiliation, there is the punishment of the Fires. After this, the one deluded by the world and heedless of the Hereafter, pursuing transient desires and fleeting pleasures, was acting as one who believes that there is no difference between the wretched one in the Fire (p-461) and the blessed one in the Garden, because he endures the swallowing of the bitter consequences of his deeds. That produced His saying, placing them in the position of one who is certain of this or one who is heedless of it, as a reminder to them of their error and an awakening from their heedlessness: ﴿Not equal are the companions of the Fire﴾, that is, in no respect whatsoever, ﴿and the companions of the Garden﴾, the Garden being the abode of the greatest bliss, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This verse is among the proofs that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever.

Since negation of equality, in itself, does not indicate which of the two is the higher, this context, together with the clues surrounding it, indicates the elevated status of the people of the Garden. He made this explicit in His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden, they﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿are the victorious﴾, those who attain every beloved thing and are saved from every hated thing. And the companions of the Fire are the ruined in both abodes, as occurred in this expedition (ghazwa) with the two groups of believers and with the Banū al-Naḍīr and those among the hypocrites who allied with them. So far apart are the two.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 59, verse 21:**

Since it has already passed in this surah, in addition to what preceded it, that the wisdom and inimitability (i'jaz) of this Qur'an are shown at times by its exact correspondence to the occasion of its revelation, a correspondence that clears away every difficulty; at times by what is witnessed of its truthfulness regarding the actions it reported would occur; at other times by the challenge it issues through its statements; and at still other times by the arrangement of each sentence with what precedes it, in a way no human being could match in any circumstance, along with other matters that speech cannot enumerate, there follows from this his saying, explaining that the cause of the separation of the two groups in the Hereafter is their separation regarding [p. 462] this Qur'an [in this world]. It is an illustration of hearts in their hardness or softness upon hearing the Qur'an, and an imagining of it, a rebuke to the hard-hearted and a praise of the tender and soft-hearted. He turns the speech to the style of greatness, because the situation requires it: ﴿Had We sent down﴾ by Our greatness, which this sending down made manifest, ﴿this Qur'an﴾, that is, the one comprising all the sciences, distinguishing between every ambiguity, and clarifying all the wisdoms, ﴿upon a mountain﴾, that is, any mountain whatsoever, ﴿you would have seen it﴾, despite its firmness and strength, O most noble of creation [if no one other than you were qualified for such a vision], ﴿humbled﴾, that is, calm, submissive upon its firmness, abased, weeping, ﴿split apart﴾, that is, split open to the utmost extent, just as the Mount (al-Tur) split apart when We manifested Our majesty to it, with less than that splendor which We displayed to Moses, peace be upon him, in its garments. ﴿Out of fear of God﴾, that is, out of great dread of the One who possesses all perfection, fearing that it might not be fulfilling what was enjoined upon it regarding the glorification of the Qur'an when it is heard. So what is wrong with the son of Adam, when God has given him reason that He did not give the mountain, that he treats its right lightly and turns away from the lessons within it? In the verse there is praise of the Prophet ﷺ for his steadfastness in what mountains cannot withstand, and blame of those who turn away, for being harder than mountains.

Since the implied meaning is a rebuke and reproach for whoever is not softened by the Qur'an, [the verse continues]: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of God and what has descended of the truth?﴾ [al-Hadid: 16]. Indeed, We have detailed for them the lawful and the unlawful, the command and the prohibition, We have made the ruling clear, We have pointed out the ambiguous, and We have related the stories, after making them intelligent and articulate. These are the stories of those who passed away, that perhaps they may take heed. Then he joins to this His saying: ﴿And these parables﴾, that is, those in which nothing contradicts anything, ﴿We set forth for people﴾, that is, those who need them, and they are the ones in whom there is wavering and disquiet, ﴿that perhaps they may reflect﴾, that is, so that their condition, in the eyes of one who observes them, becomes the condition of one from whom reflection on those parables is hoped for, so that it benefits him when reflection leads him to remembrance, and he sees the Messenger's ﷺ admonition [to him] that everything in the Qur'an has in it [witnessings] of it, so that the Book of creation and the Book of command correspond for him. Then he abstains from the animal appetites, is freed from the self's portions, adorns himself with spiritual garments, and through striving and spiritual stations arrives at the angelic attributes, and thus becomes fit for the holy stations in the lofty gardens.

When Allah, exalted is He, elevated His allies by opening the surah with belief in the unseen, and by describing Himself as the Mighty, the Wise, after declaring Himself free of the deficiencies of ta'til (the denial of the divine attributes) and of every trace of imperfection, and after descending to His servants through the causes of the attributes and actions, until He brought them to the perceptible likenesses, they became fit for annihilation (fana') in His essence and in His attributes, which necessitate awe of Him. He then raised them to reflect on the details of what He had opened with, so He said, turning away from the style of greatness to what is greater than it, by lowering the veils of might in accordance with the method of wisdom: ﴿He﴾, that is, the One whose existence is from Himself, so non-existence never applies to Him in any way at all. Therefore no one other than Him deserves the description "He," for He is the One who exists always, without beginning and without end. He is present in every heart, yet hidden by His greatness from every sense, and for this reason the mountain splits from fear of Him.

When He expressed Himself by His most specific name, He informed us of Him, out of kindness toward us and to bring Himself down to our level, by His most famous name, which is the designation of all the names, and so He said: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One worthy of worship, to whom worship alone is fitting, who is hidden in what the intellects do not encompass and cannot encompass, of the attributes of majesty, greatness and honor. Yet He manifested Himself through His actions, which cannot be matched in any way, with the utmost manifestation, and He is distinguished with the utmost distinction. No association (shirk) has ever reached Him, not in any nation of the nations, nor in any living soul. Al-Harrali said in his explanation of the names: He is the bewilderment (law) of the hearts and intellects, that is, their confusion, which they cannot grasp. Thus the creation is bound, by the unity of the name al-Ilah, to what they have attained of the unity of the name Allah [of the all-encompassing oneness (al-ahadiyyah al-ihatiyyah) - end of quote]. For this reason [His description was ﴿there is no god but He﴾, for He has no like, nothing is fitting for Him, nothing is suitable for Him, and it cannot be imagined that anything could equal Him or approach Him. Al-Ilah is the first part of the name Allah, and for this reason] no one becomes a Muslim except by affirming His oneness. So affirming His oneness is an obligation (fard), and it is the foundation of every obligatory duty, while affirming the rest of the names is a transmitted matter (naql), and it is the foundation of every supererogatory act (nafilah). Whoever affirms the oneness in all of them has perfected his religion and the blessing has been completed upon him. Otherwise he is among those who believe. If that is from him as a statement, he is protected from the fire of rulings upon the bodies in this world; and if it is knowledge, he is freed from the fire of anxiety (halac) upon the souls in this world, which is distress at the touch of harm and withholding and stinginess at the touch of good. The oneness will not be witnessed in this word, whose content is affirming the oneness of the name al-Ilah, in a beautiful manner, except after counting all the names [by knowledge]. Al-Harrali said: al-Ilah means worship, which is humbling oneself. Whoever imagines that his need is met by something and imagines that the foundation of his need is with it, humbles himself to it, and his humbling to it is then a form of deifying it. Everyone who worships what his eye can encompass has disabled his intellect from establishing the true meaning of al-Ilah, which must be unseen. So the correct meaning of al-Ilah is that He is an unseen, self-subsisting being, deserving of worship and humbling for the sake of His self-subsistence and His being free of need through Himself.

When He informed of His uniqueness, He indicated it by the sign of His deserving that, saying, placing first what is first in existence: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, the One whose knowledge of the unseen is hidden from all of His creation. And since it might be thought that describing Him as knowing the unseen is a relative matter, called unseen only relative to some people and not others, He indicated by mentioning the opposite that the intended meaning is everything that is hidden and everything that is witnessed. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and the witnessed﴾, that is, the One who exists, so that it is in a state in which some of His creatures can perceive it and become aware of it.

When He exalted Himself in the attributes of greatness and the qualities of majesty and pride, so that He became utterly hidden, He began to show mercy to the servants by descending to them and making Himself known to them through the feelings of mercy. He said, building the speech upon the pronoun to indicate that the one spoken of first is the very same one spoken of second: ﴿He is the Most Merciful﴾, that is, the One whose mercy is general. Al-Harrali, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Mercy is causing the creation to proceed in what agrees with their portion, suits their creation and their character, and the aim of their hearts. When this is specific to some, it is raḥīmiyyah (particular mercy), and when it is all-encompassing, it is raḥmāniyyah (universal mercy). And because the meaning of the name al-Raḥmān is all-encompassing [there was no existence in the creation for its complete meaning, so it did not truly apply to any of them, and for this reason His name al-Raḥmān is attached to it in the sense of its being all-encompassing - meaning, through the name Allah].

When al-Raḥīmiyyah was specific to what the divinity is pleased with, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿the Most Compassionate﴾, that is, the One who has general mercy that brings happiness outwardly, and special mercy that brings happiness inwardly. Al-Harrali said: Raḥmah (mercy) from al-Raḥīm is the specialization of the one encompassed by universal mercy with the distinction of what he is preferred with of mercy, in contrast to the one whose affair ends in His blessings, so that the requirement of the two names combines the generality of al-Raḥmāniyyah and the specialization of al-Raḥīmiyyah. When He manifested to the creation the specialness of preference, He applied to them the name al-Raḥīm, like a parent's mercy toward their children.

Since the right of the name al-Raḥīm is to establish a mercy that is not cut off, and this was not for the creation, the true al-Raḥīm is none but Allah, who, when He specializes with mercy, does not limit it. ﴿Whoever disbelieves in the false deities and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold, which has no breaking. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 256]. "Indeed Allah does not remove knowledge by snatching it away after He has given it to you." ﴿As for those who are made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift never cut off﴾ [Hud: 108]. Therefore there is no truly Raḥīm except Allah, in the sense of realized knowledge, just as there is no Raḥmān except Allah in the sense of manifest meaning.

When sovereignty (al-mulk) is the perfection of dominion over creation, by which the King restricts them to some of what they are capable of and requites them, that is, recompenses them, according to their religion, that is, according to what He has established for them of the custom of His restricting them and His judgment over them, and according to His reckoning of their minute deeds and His encompassing of their hidden states, and His knowledge of their innermost secrets, so that the full recompense is realized and thereby the perfection of sovereignty is attained. Therefore the true reality of sovereignty is not realized in one who falls short of knowledge of the secret and what is more hidden (p. 468), nor in the Reckoner who counts the weight of the smallest atom, the All-Aware of the hidden realities of existence. Thus there is in reality no King but Allah. However, since He, exalted is He, has granted some of creation an elevation above others, He has applied to them the name of King as a trial for them. Because of this, some people claimed true sovereignty, and whoever among creation intended Allah by them was misled, and they led others astray. He repeated the declaration of La ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah) along with His name al-Malik (the King), just as He began it with His name al-Ilah (the God), the first of Allah's names. For this reason too, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, in the hadith of Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), which al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi related, concerning the one who is called "King of Kings", in Muslim's narration: "There is no king but Allah." He thus stated explicitly what lies within the inner meaning of the two names of mercy of coercion and compulsion, in the first order of construction on the pronoun, as an emphasis on the definiteness of the one spoken of [and His unity]: ﴿He is Allah﴾, that is, the One who cannot generalize mercy to whomever He wills and restrict it to whomever He wishes, ﴿Besides whom there is no god﴾, that is, no one truly worthy of worship, ﴿the King﴾. So there is in reality no king but Him, because He has need of nothing; whatever He wills, it is.

Since sovereignty is the root of the afflictions that befall creation, for it is the head of nobility, which is the gate to the luxury that accompanies opposition to the Book of Allah, then in deeds it becomes a trial, and in opinion it becomes exaltation, arrogance and disbelief. The command of Allah concerning Adam was prophethood, then it descends and becomes caliphate (khilafa), then its descent ends in kingship (mulk), and then events fall apart (p. 469). Because of the instability of kingship and its requirements of blame, after the attributes of the King He said: ﴿the Holy One (al-Quddus)﴾, explicitly stating what follows from the completeness of His sovereignty: that He is supremely pure from every defect that a sense perceives, or imagination conceives, or illusion arrives at, or the heart harbours. For holiness (al-quds) is a purity that does not accept change and to which no impurity attaches. He therefore remains upon the attribute of praiseworthiness through the permanence of holiness. And because He, glorified is He, transformed creation from a state of purity in which no change appears [by what] lies beneath it, He applied to them the name of holiness, like the Holy Spirit (ruh al-quds), which supports the Lawgiver and breathes into the heart of the poet who is supported by Him in his defence of him. And for the sake of restricting the Creator's self-abandonment to sovereignty in the small provision of this world, the Prophet, the servant (ﷺ), turned away from it, and chose perpetual servitude with the lasting might of his Lord. Thus the knowledge became clear that there is no Holy One but Allah, both in true meaning and in comprehensive correctness.

Since He, glorified is He, because of the completeness of His sovereignty, the loftiness of His dominion and the perfection of His holiness, cannot be conceived to suffer any deficiency in His essence, attributes or actions, it is not foul for Him to destroy in any state, nor to touch with harm in this world or the next at any time. For He, glorified is He, by His knowledge of the outward and the inward alike, arranges matters in their most fitting places in a manner that no one else perceives at all, or does not perceive in its true perception. Therefore there is need for something that grants security from this. And peace (al-salam) was the limit between affection and separation, and the limit between mercy and force, and it is the lowest attainment of the ignorant among the servants of the Merciful, and the attainment of the transgressor from the powerful. The greeting of peace from a Muslim to the ignorant was a courtesy, lest he increase his ignorance against him, or a waiting for an opportunity to receive [a benefit]. Allah, however, does not care for creation and has no need to await any opportunity, for nothing can overcome Him. Therefore peace is not fully realized in every sense of being free from harm for Him and bestowing it upon others except from Him [as a deferral from hastening the deserving of force, and as a guarding of the sanctity of the exclusive mercy]. He followed that, granting security [to the disobedient from being hastened to punishment, and to the obedient from ill treatment], with His saying: ﴿the Source of Peace (al-Salam)﴾, for it is the limit between them outwardly. For this reason He followed it with what relates to the inward, so that the encompassing of security is realized outwardly and inwardly, and He said: ﴿the Granter of Security (al-Mu'min)﴾, because security is the limit between love and hatred toward one who has no means to love. [And it is the least that the one who has a right accepts from one who deserves love from him. For this reason he does not accept the surrender of the right from one who is apparently a means to love] except through love. Thus the faith of the believer is not established by mere belief in Him out of love for Him, but by preferring His love over every love and by equalling his brother in faith in what he loves for himself. The least of it is security [in] the unseen from backbiting and fault-finding, up to the ultimate safety from the calamities of oppression and injustice from a neighbour who is obliged to protect his neighbour in his absence. So failing in faith, by its being security in the unseen, is hypocrisy, and failing in Islam, by its being peace in confrontation, is a violation of sanctity. Thus with the least failure on the side of the Truth or of creation, Islam and faith are breached. And all of that is in reality from Allah, exalted is He, for it is He to whom security and safety are ascribed, by granting their causes and preventing the causes of fear. There is no security or safety in existence except that it is derived from Him.

Since the perception of the clear matters mentioned above, so that the meaning of peace and security may be realized, and each of those limits is very hidden, requiring further knowledge, He said: ﴿the Guardian (al-Muhaymin)﴾. For hayman is witnessing with expertise, comprehensive encompassing and seeing into the totality of the outward and inward of the matter, such that no hidden identity and no manifest outward appearance escapes Him. And because its meaning is so encompassing, it hardly ever befits being applied to creation except by way of leniency, for creation witnesses only outward appearances and does not witness the inward. For this reason its meaning became obscure to many of the eloquent Arabs. The concept of its meaning requires its oneness, which is obvious, since there is no guardian in the sense of a witness in the aforementioned manner, together with a trustworthy trust, preservation and care, except that He is standing over [every] thing with all that it has of sustenance, deed and term (p. 472), except Him. For this reason the Qur'an, which is His attribute, glorified and exalted is He, was a guardian over all the books that came before it, confirming what deserves confirmation of them and denouncing what deserves denunciation. Whoever is most skilled in it is thereby most knowledgeable.

Since complete expertise necessitates complete power, He stated this necessary implication, saying: ﴿the Almighty (al-'Aziz)﴾. And might ('izza) is a dominance in which the one overcome finds no way of resistance, escape or evasion. So the Almighty is the one whose reality is difficult for the seeker to grasp, while everything is in need of Him at every moment, the Severe in His retribution, against whom there is no one who can frustrate the execution of His judgment. For this reason He frequently combines verses of the enforcement of judgments with wisdom and knowledge, as an indication of justice. Al-Ghazali said: He is the One whose like is rarely found, the need for whom is intense, and whose attainment is difficult. Since the one who is overpowered in something, and so it is taken from his hand, may not submit inwardly, and so he does not carry out for the conqueror what he has been overcome in, and since might may not be manifest to everyone, He followed it with His saying: ﴿the Compeller (al-Jabbar)﴾, who is the Great, whose reach is beyond the opponent's grasp. He is thus among the names of the Essence, and He sets right the affairs of whomever He wills among creation and compels them to what He wills. They are too lowly to disobey Him for the blink of an eye without His will. Compulsion (al-jabr) is a bounty that forces the lower to what the higher wills from it, and what the lower seeks to attain from the higher disappears (p. 473), with complete manifestness on which its matter turns. Thus the Compeller: nothing escapes from His grasp, hands fall short of the sanctuary of the majesty of His presence, and nothing is attained from Him except what He bestows. He is the farthest thing from the attributes of creation, since the fly can attain from them what it wills while they are powerless against it. And because of the compulsion within it, it was the name that compels the Fire, restricting it to His purpose for it, by the nature He has made it to have, opposite to its nature of seeking more. So it keeps saying what it was made to say: "Is there more?", until the Compeller places His foot in it, that is, humiliates it, for the foot is the place of humiliation. [And this humiliation] is from the beginning of the manifestation of the victory of mercy over wrath. So to Him belongs sovereignty (mulk) manifestly, through the outward hands of humanity and what lies beneath it; to Him belongs dominion (malakut) inwardly, through the inward hands of sovereignty and what lies beneath it; and to Him belongs might (jabarut), exclusively, from behind every sovereignty and dominion.

Since compulsion may come through a kind of gentleness, He followed it with His saying: ﴿the Majestic (al-Mutakabbir)﴾, so that compulsion encompasses the outward and the inward. Greatness (al-kibriya') is the totality of the outward execution of Allah's command and of His outward creation, in which creatures find their smallness beneath Him and His greatness over them, and His refusal of what they wish of their wishes, because all are contemptible in relation to His majesty, the might of His compulsion, His magnificence (p. 474) and His perfection. Since all creatures are equal in the general presence of power, smallness encompassed them, so no greatness was valid for them, nor was any arrogance prescribed for them. Thus creation possesses no true share in it, nor any clothing of truth. He is specific with this name because He overpowers the outward by manifesting His greatness, through His not needing anything, and by compelling others to need Him, and by bringing down their tyrants and humiliating them, and other alarming and frightening matters without concern for anything. Likewise He is specific with the name al-Jabbar because He overpowers the inward.

Since it has been established by what was mentioned of the manifestations of His greatness that He overpowers the outward and the inward, through gentleness and harshness, this produces His exaltation above any admixture of deficiency, especially that of associating partners. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾, that is, the supreme King, who is exclusively characterized by all attributes of perfection, is exalted with a transcendence that intellects cannot grasp beyond this: that He is high above the attributes of creation, so that no deficiency can come near Him. ﴿Above what they associate﴾, that is, above these created things, [of] idols and others, whatever is on the earth or in the heavens, of great and small, of majestic and contemptible.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 59, verse 24:

When the proof of God's oneness was complete, through what had been conveyed of understanding by descending to the sovereignty and then by ascending to the greatness, and this conclusion resulted from it, He, glory be to Him, began another proof, which is at the utmost of descent and clarity. He said, opening with what He opened the first with, in the sequence of the three levels: the unseen of the unseen, then the unseen, then the manifest in its levels. (p. 475) This is to inform that there is no departure from belief in the unseen, and whoever departs from it is ruined. ﴿He﴾, that is, the One to whom no thing deserves that this pronoun [this pronoun] be applied other than Him, because His existence is from His own essence, and nothing other than Him is except that it is contingent (mumkin), so He is worthy of not existing, and so there is no manifestation for Him, so that there might be a hidden side for Him.

When He began with this pure unseen, which is the most manifest of things, He informed about it with the most famous of names, which admits no partnership in any respect, and so He said: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who has no namesake, so there is no equal to Him, and so He is the one truly intended (al-ma'hud bil-haqq), so there is no partner to Him in any respect. When He, glory be to Him, began with this comprehensive proof that unites the unseen and the manifest, He followed it with a revelation that includes knowledge and power, which is at the utmost of manifestness, and so He said: ﴿The Creator﴾, that is, the One besides whom there is no creator in the true sense, because creation is the imposition of limit and measure upon an absolute matter from which, as yet, there was no limit or measure, like the cobbler who creates (yakhluqu), that is, measures out in the leather a limit and a measure for a shoe or the like, and this is prior to the cutting and the splitting and the like. "Knowledge preceded action." So the Creator in reality is the One with whom everything is by measure, the One who says ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:6), ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We send it not down except in a known measure﴾ (Al-Hijr 15:21). From the emergence of measure comes differentiation and ordering, and from the emergence of differentiation and ordering comes giving life and causing death, and from the return of differentiation, giving life and causing death, at its first matter, comes gathering and nurturing (al-rabb). So none possesses creation and separation except one who possesses gathering and nurturing. The creatures have been given the faculty of what is in separation and dispersal, but they do not possess the gathering of what they have separated, nor the rejoining of what they have scattered, like one who cuts off a limb and cannot reattach it, or one who demolishes a building and cannot rebuild it to its previous form, or one who breaks a thing and cannot join it. Because the creatures cannot encompass the measuring of what they hasten to measure, and cannot, after separation and cutting, repair or rejoin it, He who is the encompassing of measure in a thing from all its aspects and the totality of its limits, who is able to gather what He separated, He who, as He began the first creation, will bring it back, is the best of creators. And under this ambiguity in the application of the name "Creator" [to the true Creator], there is a shimmer: the true Creator, possessor of power, might, capability, encompassment, origination and return, and [the application] to a creator from among the creatures, who is a measurer without encompassing knowledge, and without rooted power or ability, and without completing origination, and so has a share of return only in that there is no creator except Allah, just as there is no restorer of what has been originated except Allah. And the application of this name to creatures is not the cause of their trial by which He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And the realization of the individual creatures' [being] for Allah in what appears by the hands of the people of sovereignty and the dominion of the heavens, and the encompassing of His might over what appears and what is hidden of their deeds and crafts, is the first gathering point of the gatherings of monotheism (tawhid). It is the foundation of the faith of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), since He made obligatory for them in the Opening (al-Fatiha) ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ (Al-Fatiha 1:5). They are therefore the best community brought forth for mankind, since they made religion sincerely for Allah. And because shirk enters into it, the Qadariyya (the school that affirmed human power over creation) became the Magians of this community.

When the true Creator is the One who perfected measure and making, though most creatures, because of their deficiency, understand from it only absolute measurement, as their poet said:

"Indeed you split what you created, / while some people create and then do not split."

He followed it, as an alert, a clarification and an emphasis on that, with His saying: ﴿The Maker of Shapes (al-Bari')﴾, [that is], the One who refines what measure has fallen upon, cuts it and sets it right to receive the form in its most complete condition. If He is one whose knowledge encompasses, it is the complete preparedness for the form with perfect will in it. And if He is one whose knowledge does not encompass, there occurs to him in making, from the deficiency that prevents completion, what makes the attainment of the intended goal in the form impossible. And benefaction to creatures in their made things hardly occurs except by agreement, whose reality they do not know and in whose occurrence they are not confident.

When the one who prepares matters for shaping may not perfect it, He said: ﴿The Fashioner (al-Musawwir)﴾. (p. 478) For shaping is the completion of the detailing of the outward creation, the perfecting of its outline and the strengthening of its limbs, and it is the limit of what creation reaches in manifestness. Beyond the manifestation of forms there is no further existence except the subtleties of their refinement in attaining the perfection of their maturity after their raising, by giving them life through what they have of the spirit that sustains them, whether animal or otherwise, until the final perfection which the Fashioner gives them by bounty and increase, and manifests by originating. The difference between the three names becomes very clear through building. For it first requires one who measures what is necessary of stone, brick, wood and iron, the area of the land, the number of structures, their length and width, and this the engineer undertakes, and draws it, and this is the creating. Then it requires a stonecutter who carves the stones and prepares them to fit the places where they will be, such as the doors, the middles and edges and corners of walls and other things, and likewise the carpenter and the blacksmith for the wood and iron, and this is the making. Then the mason takes the whole and places it in its places until its form stands as the engineer first drew and measured it. The form does not stand in truth unless it is firmly made to the extent of capacity, just as the mason places the stones first and then sets the wood above them, not by chance but by wisdom. Were this reversed, the form would not stand and would not deserve the name except in the weakest of respects. So whoever is more firm, his shaping is greater. Therefore (p. 479) there is no true Fashioner except Allah, the Creator, the Maker of Shapes, the Fashioner, glory be to Him. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': "Shaping exists in every part of the world, however small, even in the atom and the ant, indeed in every limb of the ant. Indeed the discussion would be long concerning the layers of the eye, their number, their forms, their shape, their measures, their colors, and the wisdom in them. Whoever does not know its form does not know its Fashioner except by the general name. The same is true of the form of every animal and plant, indeed of every part of a plant and an animal."

When it became known from this that the Fashioner must be one of perfect wisdom, He followed it with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾, that is, exclusively, not to another, ﴿the Most Beautiful Names﴾, that is, from the Wise and others, of whom the shaping is not complete without Him, and whom you do not comprehend [as you should] in true comprehension.

When He, glory be to Him, informed at the beginning of the surah that the beings brought into existence His glorification, in submission to His might and wisdom, and indicated that by what preceded until He made the attentive ears hear the Most Beautiful Names, He indicated the continuation of the attribute of [this] for one who needs reminding among the creatures, because of his deficiency. So He used the present tense and said: ﴿Glorifies﴾, that is, repeats the supreme declaration of transcendence from every trace of deficiency, in the manner of renewal and continuity. ﴿To Him﴾, that is, in the manner of specification, which is conveyed by restricting the transitive verb and its being made transitive by the preposition li- [to]. ﴿Whatever is in the heavens﴾. And since this One who is declared transcendent, Whose transcendence is disclosed through the Most Beautiful Names, has had His breaths shine and His regions and plantings become refined, until he becomes of the heavenly realm, he sees the earth as lofty like the heavens, because it shares with them in indicating the perfection of His completeness. So He placed it with them, because one does not need to repeat, like a single thing, by dropping "mā," and joined it to them as an allusion to that, and said: ﴿and the earth﴾. Whoever contemplates existence, in general and in detail, knows the glorification of all of it through attributes of perfection and qualities of majesty and beauty. ﴿And He﴾, that is, while He alone is ﴿the Mighty﴾, [that is], the One who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything, has no like, is difficult to reach, and is greatly needed.

When one who has this attribute does not complete his affair, nor does everything he wills become firm, unless he is upon the law of wisdom, He said: ﴿the Wise﴾, from wisdom, which is the firm perfecting of judgment and bringing it to a limit that cannot be annulled. Judgment, al-Harrali said, is the restraining from what the judged is inclined toward, governing over it and carrying him toward what he refuses, for his sake. Its outward aspect is hardship, its inward aspect is gentleness; in its immediate aspect it is disliked, and in its end is contentment and relief. Its place in bodies is treatment: "Treat yourselves, servants of Allah, for the One who sent down the disease also sent down the cure." Its place in religions is the adherence to rulings, patience, perseverance in struggling against deeds and fighting enemies, outwardly against the enemy of religion and transgression, and inwardly against the enemy of the self: "The most hostile of your enemies is your self which is between your sides" (p. 481). And some of one's family and children are enemies, and Satan is an enemy who runs in the son of Adam like the blood: ﴿Indeed Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ (Fatir 35:6). So the bearing of all kinds of patience and perseverance, outwardly by lofty governance, is judgment, and knowledge of the matter for whose sake judgment became obligatory, from the sustaining of the affair of the immediate life and the goodness of the outcome in the end, is wisdom. Thus judgment is permitted to be taught to people generally, and indeed it is obligatory that every person learn the rulings that concern him, and that a group be appointed to know what concerns all people: ﴿Why did not a group from every section of them go forth to gain understanding in religion?﴾ (At-Tawba 9:122). And wisdom, which is the knowledge of that for whose sake judgment became obligatory, has as its condition teaching with purification: ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were in clear error﴾ (Al-Jumu'a 62:2). [So he does not teach them wisdom] except after purification. Whoever purifies himself is of its people, and whoever does not purify himself is not of its people. So wisdom sweetens the bitterness of the effort of acting by the rulings, and by it what is difficult without it becomes easy. And judgment is the narrowness of the affair for the self, just as prison is the narrowness of space for the body. And wisdom firmly establishes the bearing of the narrowness of judgment, because it comes out and returns to the breadth of the Expansive. Judgment is not completed, and wisdom is not made level, except in proportion to the breadth of knowledge.

And since creatures have no knowledge except to the measure that Allah bestows upon them, they have no wisdom except the measure that it bequeaths to them: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾ (Luqman 31:12). (p. 482) And since knowledge is only with Allah, wisdom is only the wisdom of Allah, and judgment is only the judgment of Allah. He is the Wise, besides whom there is no wise one. [End.] The secret of following the noble names without a conjunction has become known. That is because He began with "Huwa" and informed about Him with the great, singular, guarded proper name that comprehends all the meanings of the Most Beautiful Names, then followed it with those exalted attributes without a conjunction, to inform that none of them conveys all of its meaning according to the understanding commonly held among the people of the language. For this reason, after them He gathered the names, as an indication that its meaning is gathered only by all the attributes revealed in His books and taken from His friends, which He has reserved in His unseen. None of what is mentioned here is opposed, in its outward meaning, to the other, like the First and the Last, so that a deficiency in meaning might be suspected because of the omission of the conjunction. As for its arrangement in this way, it is because each name, as has passed, explains what is hidden in the one before it, clarifies its implications, and makes clear what has become evident from its content. And the end of it has bent back to its beginning, and its beginning has embraced its completion, and its opening has fulfilled its closing, and it has increased and reached the goal of guidance to the path of rectitude. Glory be to Him who sent it down by His mercy as a mercy to His servants, and as a guide to what is right and sound.
